questions.stem: Which practice violates the ASA basic monitoring standard for circulation?
options: Cycling NIBP every 6 minutes during stable maintenance
Displaying the ECG continuously until preparing to leave the room
Cycling NIBP every 3 minutes during induction
Confirming circulation with pulse oximetry plethysmography
questions.explanation: Arterial BP and HR must be determined and evaluated at least every 5 minutes. The highlighted slide note says it may be less than 5 but never more. ECG must be continuously displayed from the start of anesthesia until preparing to leave, and pleth or oximetry is an accepted additional circulation check.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 13, 60 (PDF p. 13, 61)

questions.stem: Which monitor would catch a vaporizer that was never turned on at the start of a case?
options: Expired anesthetic agent analysis
The low-pressure system leak check
The vaporizer's sight glass fill level
The machine's low agent-level alert
questions.explanation: Slide 69: the machine may alert to low agent LEVELS, but there is NO alert for vaporizer operation. A full sight glass looks the same whether the dial is on or off. Only the gas analyzer's agent reading shows no agent is being delivered. The leak check catches a loose filler cap, not a vaporizer left off.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 69 (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Five minutes after an extremity tourniquet is released, ETCO2 rises from 35 to 43 mmHg, then drifts back toward baseline. What best explains this?
options: Washout of CO2 from the previously ischemic limb
Worsening bronchospasm trapping CO2 in the alveoli
Early malignant hyperthermia from volatile exposure
Exhausted CO2 absorbent causing rebreathing
questions.explanation: The lecture lists transient ETCO2 increases after tourniquet release, aortic unclamping, or bicarbonate. The key word is transient: CO2 built up in the limb returns to the circulation and is exhaled. MH produces a sustained, progressive rise, and an exhausted absorbent raises the inspiratory baseline.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 41, 45 (PDF p. 41, 46)

questions.stem: Which actions increase the risk of overfilling a variable bypass vaporizer? Select 2.
options: Filling while the vaporizer dial is on
Filling with the vaporizer turned off
Filling only to the marked maximum line
Keeping the vaporizer upright on the manifold while filling
Confirming the agent-specific key before filling
Filling with the bottle key not tightly seated
questions.explanation: Slide 70: overfilling comes from filling while the vaporizer is on, in the wrong position, or with the key not tight on the bottle. It risks contaminating the bypass chamber or outlet and overdosing the patient. Fill with the vaporizer off, upright, to the specified level, and don't fill until it stops bubbling.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 70 (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Which anesthesia technique errors contaminate the OR with waste gas? Select 3.
options: Turning off fresh gas flow before disconnecting the circuit
Disconnecting a deeply anesthetized patient from the circuit at the end of the case
Using the pause fresh gas flow function during intubation
Leaving N2O and the vaporizer on while the mask is off for intubation
Spilling liquid agent while refilling a vaporizer
Using a cuffed tube appropriately sized for the trachea
questions.explanation: Technique errors cause 94-99% of OR contamination. Gas left flowing while disconnected, disconnecting a deep patient who keeps exhaling agent, and spills (about 200 mL of vapor per mL of liquid) all add to room levels. Pausing or turning off fresh gas and using a well-fitting cuffed tube are the lecture's fixes, not errors.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which statements about removable galvanic O2 sensors are correct? Select 2.
options: Exposure to CO2 extends its life
The sensor is consumed over time
It works by oxygen's attraction to a magnetic field
It is calibrated against room air (21%) daily
It directly measures arterial PaO2
It reliably detects breathing circuit disconnection
questions.explanation: Galvanic cells generate current from an O2-dependent chemical reaction, so the sensor is consumed. They're calibrated to room air (21%) daily and after prolonged use. CO2 SHORTENS sensor life, paramagnetic analyzers are the ones using magnetism, and inspired O2 alarms don't reliably detect disconnection.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 35, 36, 38 (PDF p. 35, 36, 38)

questions.stem: Why is a recirculating OR ventilation system a concern for waste anesthetic gas exposure?
options: Filters don't remove anesthetic gases, so air can carry them between ORs
It provides fewer than 3 air exchanges per hour in each OR
It shuts off the scavenging vacuum while recirculating air
It pulls waste gas back into the anesthesia machine circuit
questions.explanation: A recirculating system mixes fresh outdoor air with filtered, conditioned stale air, but the filters don't clean out anesthetic gases, so contaminated air can move to clean ORs. ORs need 15-21 exchanges per hour with at least 3 fresh. When OR ventilation is used for passive disposal, it must be nonrecirculating.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 17, 21 (PDF p. 9, 11)

questions.stem: When available, which method does the AANA standard recommend for assessing recovery from neuromuscular blockade?
options: Tactile assessment of fade during 50 Hz tetanic stimulation
A sustained 5-second head lift before extubation
Quantitative monitoring such as acceleromyography with a TOF ratio
Visual count of train-of-four twitches at the adductor pollicis
questions.explanation: NM response must be monitored whenever NMBAs are given, and quantitative monitoring (acceleromyography, TOF ratio) is recommended when available. Instructor note: quantitative vs qualitative, pick quantitative. Visual and tactile methods are qualitative.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 15 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: An arterial line reads 188/60 while a correctly sized cuff reads 162/64. A fast-flush test shows several rapid oscillations before the waveform settles. What explains the difference?
options: Underdamping, which overestimates systolic pressure
A transducer mounted above the heart
Underdamping, which underestimates systolic pressure
Overdamping, which overestimates systolic pressure
questions.explanation: The fast-flush test assesses resonant oscillations and dynamic response. Multiple oscillations after the flush mean an underdamped system, which overestimates SBP by 15-30 mmHg and amplifies artifacts. Overdamping underestimates SBP, and a transducer above the heart reads falsely low overall.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 65, 69 (PDF p. 66, 70)

questions.stem: A variable bypass vaporizer was tipped while being moved out of transport mode. Which statements are correct? Select 2.
options: Output returns to normal once the wicks re-saturate
Management: drain, run highest setting at high FGF for about 30 min, refill when analysis reads zero
Refilling to the top of the sight glass rebalances the splitting ratio
Liquid agent can enter the bypass chamber and raise vaporizer output
It is safe to use once upright if the dial is set lower
Output falls because the wicks are no longer saturated
questions.explanation: Tipping lets liquid into the bypass chamber, which increases output and risks overdose. The fix on slide 71: drain the vaporizer, run the highest setting with high FGF for 30 minutes, and refill once expired gas analysis no longer detects agent. Output doesn't fall, and it doesn't self-correct; turning the dial down doesn't make it safe while the bypass is contaminated.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 71 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: During an apneic period, SpO2 falls from 97% to 90%. Why is this a critical point?
options: PaO2 is near 90 mmHg, so a large reserve remains
PaO2 is near 60 mmHg, on the steep part of the curve where desaturation speeds up
Pulse oximeter accuracy is lost below 90%
The curve has shifted left, so O2 unloading to tissues improves
questions.explanation: Instructor note: a PaO2 of 60 is about 90%, and it drops quickly after this. Once PaO2 reaches the steep portion of the sigmoid curve, desaturation can accelerate rapidly. Accuracy is about 2-3% from 70-100% saturation, so the reading below 90% is still usable.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 76 (PDF p. 77)

questions.stem: Why is desflurane delivered by a heated, pressurized vaporizer instead of a standard variable bypass design?
options: Its boiling point is far above room temperature, so it won't vaporize unheated
Its boiling point (22.8 C) is near room temperature, so output would fluctuate
Its high blood:gas coefficient requires more precise delivery
Its vapor pressure is lower than sevoflurane's, so the chamber can't saturate
questions.explanation: Des has a vapor pressure of 669 mmHg and boils at 22.8 C, so near room temperature it can boil. Heating to 39 C and pressurizing to 2 atm keeps it predictable and minimizes output swings. Its boiling point is low, not high; its vapor pressure is far higher than sevo's (160); and its blood:gas coefficient (0.42) is the lowest listed.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 60 (PDF p. 25, 30)

questions.stem: A closed-reservoir scavenging interface is attached to hospital vacuum that is set too high. What protects the breathing circuit from negative pressure?
options: The interface reservoir bag distends to buffer the suction
The positive-pressure (pop-off) relief valve opens to the room
The negative-pressure (pop-in) relief valve opens and lets room air in
Nothing; the negative pressure is transmitted to the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: In a closed interface, excessive vacuum opens the pop-in valve so room air enters the reservoir, protecting the circuit. The pop-off valve opens the other way, when vacuum FAILS and pressure builds, venting gas to the room. With too much suction the reservoir bag collapses rather than distends. The open interface (most common) is valveless with ports open to atmosphere.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: The lecture separates clinical from objective signs of adequate bag-mask ventilation. Which are objective signs? Select 3.
options: Exhaled tidal volume
Visible chest movement
Waveform exhaled CO2
Sustained oxygen saturation
Size of the gas leak around the mask
Lip color seen through the clear mask
questions.explanation: Objective measures listed: sustained SpO2, waveform exhaled CO2, peak airway pressure, and exhaled tidal volume. Chest movement and mask leak are the clinical signs. The clear mask lets you watch lips, condensation (instructor: watch the amount of fog), secretions, vomit, and blood, but those are observations, not objective measures.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: During one-lung ventilation, an ABG shows PaCO2 56 mmHg while ETCO2 reads 33 mmHg. What best explains the gap?
options: A normal gradient, since up to 25 mmHg is expected
Hypoventilation, which widens the PaCO2-ETCO2 gradient
Rebreathing CO2 from an exhausted absorbent
Increased alveolar dead space widening the gradient
questions.explanation: The normal gradient is about 5 mmHg (range 2-10). One-lung ventilation is on the lecture's list of situations where ETCO2 underestimates PaCO2, because ventilated but poorly perfused alveoli dilute the exhaled CO2. Hypoventilation raises both values without widening the gap, and rebreathing raises ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 40, 49 (PDF p. 40, 50)
questions.disc: The handwritten note on slide 40 attributes the normal 5 mmHg gap to anatomic dead space. Sources differ on the normal gap, but agree that WIDENING of the gradient (PE, low CO, OLV) comes from alveolar dead space, which is what this question tests.

questions.stem: Before induction, what endpoint does the lecture give for adequate preoxygenation?
options: ETCO2 below 35 mmHg after 3 minutes of mask breathing
Expired O2 at least 90%, or 3-5 minutes of 100% O2 with a tight seal
Inspired O2 of at least 90% for 1 minute with a mask
SpO2 of 100% held for at least 1 minute on the mask
questions.explanation: Pre-induction: mask seal with FiO2 100% for 3-5 minutes or until expired O2 is at least 90%. Expired O2 is the marker because it reflects lung denitrogenation. Inspired O2 only shows what the machine delivers, and SpO2 can hit 100% long before the lungs are filled with O2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 91 (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: Absorbent that was purple at the end of Friday's last case looks white on Monday morning. Within 20 minutes of the first case, the capnogram baseline no longer returns to zero. What best explains this?
options: Weekend gas flow restored the absorbent's capacity
The indicator regenerated at rest, so exhausted absorbent looked usable
Ethyl violet turns from purple to white as absorbent is exhausted
A sampling calibration error, since the absorbent looks fresh
questions.explanation: Ethyl violet goes white to purple with exhaustion, and the color can fade back at rest (regeneration) even though the hydroxides are used up. The highlighted slide point: color change is not to be relied on. Instructor note: some purple turns back white at the end of the day, so check and change it. A baseline above zero means rebreathing.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 2, 4 (PDF p. 1, 2)

questions.stem: On this normal capnogram, which segment represents alveolar gas being sampled?
options: A to B
B to C
C to D
D to E
questions.explanation: A to B is anatomic dead space with essentially no CO2. B to C is the expiratory upstroke as CO2-containing gas arrives. C to D is the alveolar (expiratory) plateau, when alveolar gas is sampled. D is ETCO2, the best reflection of alveolar CO2. D to E is the inspiratory downstroke as fresh gas is entrained.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 44 (PDF p. 44)

questions.stem: Which components belong to the anesthesia machine's high-pressure system? Select 3.
options: Hanger yoke
Flow control valve
O2 fail-safe valve
Pipeline inlet check valve
Yoke check valve
Cylinder (Bourdon) pressure gauge
questions.explanation: The high-pressure system handles cylinder gas from the yoke up to the first-stage regulator: hanger yoke, cylinder, cylinder gauge, and yoke check valve. Pipeline inlets, the fail-safe, and the flush valve are intermediate-pressure components. Flow control valves are the dividing line into the low-pressure system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 6, 22, 23, 26 (PDF p. 3, 11, 12, 13)

questions.stem: This pressure-volume loop appears during mechanical ventilation. What does it indicate?
options: A leak in the breathing circuit
Decreased compliance from insufflation
Increased airway resistance during expiration
Abnormally increased lung compliance
questions.explanation: The loop doesn't close: the expiratory limb never returns to the starting volume, because some delivered volume isn't coming back. That's an open loop from a circuit leak. Bronchospasm widens a closed loop, increased compliance (emphysema) makes the loop tall and steep toward the volume axis, and decreased compliance shifts it toward the pressure axis.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 29 (PDF p. 29)

questions.stem: Which ventilator alarms serve as disconnect alarms? Select 3.
options: Low exhaled tidal volume
Low exhaled CO2
Low O2 supply pressure
Low peak inspiratory pressure
High PEEP
High peak inspiratory pressure
questions.explanation: There are at least three disconnect alarms: low PIP, low exhaled tidal volume, and low exhaled CO2. A small leak or partial disconnect may show up first as subtle drops in these values before any alarm threshold is crossed. High PIP, high PEEP, and low O2 supply pressure are separate alarms.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 33 (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: Sevoflurane runs at 2% with 2 L/min fresh gas flow for one hour. About how much liquid agent is used?
options: 6 mL
12 mL
24 mL
40 mL
questions.explanation: From the lecture: liquid used (mL/hr) = vol% x FGF (L/min) x 3. So 2 x 2 x 3 = 12 mL/hr. The factor of 3 reflects that 1 mL of liquid makes about 200 mL of vapor.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: O2 pipeline pressure falls to 35 psig during a case. The O2 E-cylinder on the machine was left open. What happens?
options: The machine keeps drawing from the pipeline because pipeline gas has priority
O2 flow stops until pipeline pressure returns above 50 psig
The fail-safe valve shuts off O2 because pressure is below 50 psig
The machine starts drawing O2 from the cylinder, which may empty
questions.explanation: The cylinder's first-stage regulator delivers about 45 psi, and the pipeline normally runs 50-55 psi. The machine uses the higher-pressure source, which is why the cylinder normally stays as backup. At 35 psig the regulated cylinder pressure is now higher, so the cylinder takes over and can empty without anyone noticing. The fail-safe acts on the other gases, not on O2.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 24, 33 (PDF p. 12, 17)

questions.stem: Which finding is typically the earliest monitor sign of malignant hyperthermia?
options: Fall in ETCO2 from increased dead space
Rise in core temperature
Unexplained rise in ETCO2
Fall in SpO2
questions.explanation: MH increases CO2 production, so the analyzer table lists it under CO2 and Box 18.1 lists it first among causes of increased ETCO2. Instructor note: the temperature change is a LATE sign of MH. ETCO2 rises, not falls.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 42, 43, 84 (PDF p. 42, 43, 85)

questions.stem: In a 3-year-old, after the head is repositioned, SpO2 drifts from 99% to 93%. The capnogram looks unchanged, and PIP and plateau both rise. What is most likely?
options: Bronchospasm from airway manipulation
Partial circuit disconnection at the Y-piece
Exhausted CO2 absorbent in the canister
Mainstem (endobronchial) intubation
questions.explanation: Endobronchial intubation is on the lecture's list of causes of increased PIP AND plateau. In pediatrics, pulse oximetry is more sensitive than capnography for unrecognized mainstem intubation, which fits a falling SpO2 with an unchanged capnogram. Bronchospasm raises PIP alone and changes the capnogram shape; disconnection drops pressures.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 32, 78 (PDF p. 32, 79)

questions.stem: After hanging a new O2 E-cylinder and opening the valve, you hear a hiss at the yoke. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Open the valve fully so cylinder pressure seats the washer
Tighten the T-handle as far as it will turn with the valve open
Close the valve, reseat with a single washer, and leak-check with soapy water
Add a second washer to improve the seal, then reopen the valve
questions.explanation: The lecture's cylinder exchange steps: use only ONE washer, listen for hissing, check for leaks with soapy water, don't overtighten, and check system pressure. Stacking washers breaks the one-washer rule, and cranking the T-handle is the overtightening the slide warns against.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: How does a Macintosh blade expose the glottis?
options: Its tip in the vallecula presses the epiglottis down against the tongue base
Its tip traps the epiglottis directly and lifts it
Its tip lifts the corniculate cartilages to open the glottis
Its tip in the vallecula tensions the glossoepiglottic ligament and lifts the epiglottis
questions.explanation: The curved Mac sits in the vallecula and lifts the epiglottis indirectly by stretching the glossoepiglottic ligament. Trapping the epiglottis directly is the straight Miller blade's technique (epiglottic entrapment).
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 11 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: The tongue and soft palate are the main sources of upper airway obstruction. Which make up the triple airway maneuver? Select 3.
options: Neck flexion
Head extension
Cricoid pressure
Chin lift
A roll under the shoulders
Jaw thrust
questions.explanation: The triple airway maneuver is chin lift, head extension, and jaw thrust. Together they pull the tongue and soft palate away from the posterior pharynx. Cricoid pressure doesn't relieve soft tissue obstruction, neck flexion worsens it, and a shoulder roll is a positioning aid rather than part of the maneuver.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: In Landesberg's vascular surgery study, which lead detected perioperative ischemia earliest and most often?
options: Lead II
V5
V3
V4
questions.explanation: V3 was most sensitive (86.8%), V4 second (78.9%), and V5 third (65.8%). 97% of ischemic events showed ST depression, not elevation. Instructor note: monitor lead II for rhythm and V3 for ischemia. V5 is the classic trap answer.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 58 (PDF p. 59)

questions.stem: On a machine with a proportioning (hypoxic guard) system, N2O is set at 4 L/min and O2 is turned down toward 0.5 L/min. What does the system do?
options: Adds medical air automatically to raise the delivered FiO2
Shuts off N2O completely once O2 flow drops below 1 L/min
Alarms but allows the hypoxic mixture to be delivered
Links the N2O and O2 controls so the mixture stays above about 25% O2
questions.explanation: The proportioning system (O2 ratio controller, hypoxic guard) links O2 and N2O at the flow control valves so FiO2 stays greater than about 25% whenever N2O is used. Cutting N2O off entirely is the fail-safe responding to low O2 supply pressure, a different device.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 45 (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: What are the correct bladder dimensions for an NIBP cuff?
options: Width about 50% and length about 50% of arm circumference
Width about 20% and length about 100% of arm circumference
Width about 80% and length about 40% of arm circumference
Width about 40% and length at least 80% of arm circumference
questions.explanation: Highlighted on slide 61: internal bladder width 40% and length 80% (covering 75-100%) of upper arm circumference. Slide 90 repeats width about 40% and length at least 80%.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 61, 90 (PDF p. 62, 91)
questions.disc: The handwritten note on slide 90 reverses these numbers (80% circumference, 40% length). Both slides themselves say width 40%, length 80%, so this question is keyed to the slides.

questions.stem: The capnogram's inspiratory baseline no longer returns to zero. Which problems could cause this? Select 3.
options: Hyperventilation lowering the end-tidal value
Bronchospasm slowing the expiratory upstroke
Chemically exhausted CO2 absorbent
Esophageal intubation with fading waveforms
Insufficient fresh gas flow
An incompetent unidirectional valve
questions.explanation: A nonzero inspiratory baseline means CO2 is being rebreathed. Slide 50 lists an exhausted absorber, a malfunctioning ventilator circuit valve, insufficient fresh gas flow, or incorrect calibration. Bronchospasm changes the upstroke shape, esophageal intubation produces a fading or absent trace, and hyperventilation lowers ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 50, 51 (PDF p. 51, 52)

questions.stem: Where does the tip of a Macintosh blade sit during laryngoscopy?
options: Label A
Label B
Label C
Label D
questions.explanation: B is the vallecula, the space between the base of the tongue and the epiglottis. Seating the Mac tip there tensions the glossoepiglottic ligament (D on this slide) to lift the epiglottis (C) indirectly. A is the tongue. Instructor note: know the anatomy.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 2, 11 (PDF p. 2, 11)

questions.stem: A patient with confirmed methemoglobinemia is breathing 100% O2, and an ABG shows PaO2 420 mmHg, but SpO2 reads 86%. How should the pulse oximeter reading be interpreted?
options: Falsely low, because MetHb absorbs red and infrared light about equally
Falsely low, because carboxyhemoglobin reads as reduced hemoglobin
Accurate, reflecting true desaturation despite the high PaO2
Falsely high, because MetHb absorbs only infrared light
questions.explanation: MetHb absorbs red (660 nm) and infrared (940 nm) light in a 1:1 ratio, which the oximeter reads as about 85%. With a true saturation near 100%, 86% is falsely low. Co-oximetry uses multiple wavelengths to measure MetHb and COHb directly.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 75 (PDF p. 76)
questions.disc: Slide 75 says MetHb readings are underestimated above 70% and overestimated below 70%. Standard references (e.g., OpenAnesthesia) put the crossover at 85%, matching the slide's own 1:1 = about 85% point. This explanation uses 85%.

questions.stem: What do the notches marked by arrows on this capnogram indicate?
options: Rebreathing from an incompetent expiratory valve
A leak around the endotracheal tube cuff
Cardiac oscillations from contraction of the heart and great vessels
Spontaneous inspiratory effort out of sync with controlled ventilation
questions.explanation: These are curare clefts: dips in the alveolar plateau when the patient tries to breathe against the ventilator. Instructor note: the patient is breathing spontaneously, so consider more paralytic. Cardiac oscillations are small ripples caused by contraction of the heart and great vessels; rebreathing raises the baseline; a leak slopes the trace.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 47 (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: Midway through a case, the N2O E-cylinder gauge reads 745 psig. What can you conclude about the remaining contents?
options: The liquid phase is gone and only gaseous N2O remains
The cylinder is about half full, since pressure falls linearly with use
Liquid N2O remains, but the gauge can't show how much; weigh the cylinder
The cylinder is essentially full, holding about 1590 L of N2O
questions.explanation: N2O's critical temperature is about 36 C, so at room temperature it stays liquid under pressure. Liquid and gas sit in equilibrium and the gauge holds at 745 psig until the last liquid vaporizes. Anything from full to nearly empty can read 745, which is why the instructor noted you have to weigh the cylinder. The linear pressure-volume rule applies to O2 and air, not N2O.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Monday's first case is a desflurane anesthetic. The O2 flowmeter was found running at 10 L/min all weekend. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Proceed, because barium hydroxide lime prevents CO formation
Switch from desflurane to isoflurane
Replace the absorbent before starting
Increase fresh gas flow to wash out any CO
questions.explanation: High O2 flow over a weekend desiccates the absorbent, and dry absorbent with des produces the most CO (des > enflurane > iso). The recommendation is not to use absorbent known or suspected to be desiccated. Iso still produces CO, and Baralyme produces MORE CO than soda lime.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 6, 7 (PDF p. 3, 4)

questions.stem: After pipeline repairs, a patient desaturates with the O2 flowmeter set to 100%. O2 pipeline pressure reads 52 psig. Which device is most likely to reveal the problem?
options: The O2 analyzer in the inspiratory limb
The pipeline pressure gauge
The O2/N2O proportioning system
The O2 fail-safe valve
questions.explanation: Crossed pipelines or nitrogen contamination leave pressure normal. The fail-safe and proportioning system have no sense of O2 itself, only pressure, so neither reacts, and the gauge reads a normal 52 psig. Only the inspired O2 analyzer measures concentration. The lecture cites a 2024 crossed-pipeline case and a 2019 nitrogen contamination event.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 45, 46 (PDF p. 23); Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 36 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: With a Macintosh blade seated in the vallecula, a long, floppy epiglottis still hides the glottis. Which change directly addresses this?
options: Switch to a Miller blade to trap the epiglottis directly
Switch to a larger Macintosh blade to lift the tongue further
Insert an OPA to lift the tongue off the epiglottis
Move the head from sniffing to neutral
questions.explanation: The Mac relies on tensioning the glossoepiglottic ligament, which may not lift a long, floppy epiglottis. The Miller is a long, straight blade whose tip picks up the epiglottis directly (epiglottic entrapment), exposing the larynx regardless of how the ligament behaves.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 11 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: During volume-controlled ventilation, the O2 flush is held through an inspiration and the high peak pressure alarm sounds. Which flush hazard does this alarm reflect?
options: Light anesthesia from diluted volatile agent
Barotrauma from 35-75 L/min entering the circuit
A hypoxic mixture from bypassing the flowmeters
Higher vaporizer output from the pumping effect
questions.explanation: The flush sends O2 straight from the intermediate system to the common gas outlet at 35-75 L/min and 40-50 psi, bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers. A peak pressure alarm during mechanical inspiration points to barotrauma. Dilution of agent is the flush's other listed risk, but it doesn't raise airway pressure. The flush is 100% O2, so it can't create a hypoxic mixture.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 36, 37 (PDF p. 18, 19)

questions.stem: A patient's preoperative 12-lead ECG shows baseline ST changes in leads III and aVF. How should intraoperative lead selection be guided?
options: Prioritize III and aVF, using the patient's ECG fingerprint
Monitor lead II alone to avoid false ST alarms
Monitor V5 alone, as the standard ischemia lead
Use a three-lead system to reduce artifact
questions.explanation: Lead selection should follow the patient's history and preoperative 12-lead 'fingerprinting.' The lecture's example: if baseline changes are in III and aVF, prioritize those leads. Single-lead monitoring is inadequate for patients at risk of ischemia, and a three-lead system has limited sensitivity.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 58 (PDF p. 59)

questions.stem: Under volume control, PIP rises from 22 to 38 cmH2O while plateau pressure stays at 18. What is the most likely cause?
options: Endobronchial intubation
Steep Trendelenburg positioning
Peritoneal insufflation
Bronchospasm
questions.explanation: PIP reflects dynamic compliance (resistance plus compliance); plateau reflects static compliance. A rise in PIP with no change in plateau means higher airway resistance or inspiratory flow: bronchospasm, a kinked tube, secretions. Insufflation, Trendelenburg, and endobronchial intubation lower compliance and raise BOTH pressures.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 26, 32 (PDF p. 26, 32)

questions.stem: A variable bypass vaporizer delivers 1% sevoflurane at 2 L/min at 20 C, where sevo vapor is 21% of the sump gas. What is the approximate splitting ratio of bypass flow to sump inflow?
options: About 4:1
About 21:1
About 25:1
About 100:1
questions.explanation: 1% of about 2100 mL total is 21 mL of sevo vapor. Sump outflow is 21% sevo, so 79 mL of carrier gas must enter the sump to pick up 21 mL. The remaining 2000 mL bypasses. 2000:79 is about 25:1. 21:1 confuses the sump concentration with the ratio.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 55 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: Which conditions shift the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the right? Select 3.
options: Alkalosis
Hypocapnia
Hyperthermia
Hypercapnia
Hypothermia
Acidosis
questions.explanation: Right shifts come from hypercapnia, acidosis, and hyperthermia. They reduce hemoglobin's O2 affinity and improve O2 delivery to tissues. Hypothermia, alkalosis, and hypocapnia shift the curve left, so hemoglobin holds O2 more tightly.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 74 (PDF p. 75)

questions.stem: In soda lime, sodium carbonate reacts with which compound to regenerate sodium hydroxide?
options: Water, forming carbonic acid
Potassium hydroxide, forming potassium carbonate
Carbonic acid, forming sodium bicarbonate
Calcium hydroxide, forming calcium carbonate
questions.explanation: The sequence: CO2 + H2O makes H2CO3; H2CO3 + 2NaOH makes Na2CO3 + 2H2O (the most common reaction); then Na2CO3 + Ca(OH)2 makes CaCO3 + 2NaOH. The instructor said to expect this as a board question in the form 'what does X react with to form Y.'
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 3 (PDF p. 2)
questions.disc: Slide 3 prints calcium hydroxide as Ca(OH). The correct formula is Ca(OH)2, which is what this question uses.

questions.stem: Right after peritoneal insufflation, PIP rises from 20 to 30 cmH2O and plateau from 16 to 26. What does this pattern indicate?
options: A kinked endotracheal tube
Increased airway resistance
Decreased pulmonary compliance
Increased inspiratory flow rate
questions.explanation: When PIP and plateau rise together (the gap between them stays about the same), the cause is a larger tidal volume or decreased pulmonary compliance. Insufflation is on the lecture's list of compliance causes. Resistance problems (kink, bronchospasm) raise PIP alone.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 26, 32 (PDF p. 26, 32)

questions.stem: Right after a new absorbent canister is installed, the machine fails its low-pressure leak test. What is the most likely cause?
options: Absorbent granules on the gasket or an improperly seated canister
A loose O2 cylinder in its hanger yoke assembly
A cracked glass tube in the O2 flowmeter bank
A defective quick connect on the N2O pipeline hose
questions.explanation: Low-pressure leaks happen most often at the CO2 absorber: loose screws, worn gaskets, granules on the gaskets, or an open petcock. Instructor notes: improperly seated canisters, and a canister not seated correctly after changing can leak. Quick connects and yokes are high-pressure leaks.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 4, 13 (PDF p. 2, 7)

questions.stem: The O2 pipeline fails and you plan to switch the patient to the auxiliary O2 flowmeter. Why isn't this a dependable backup?
options: It can only deliver up to about 2 L/min
It shuts off automatically when O2 supply pressure falls
It is supplied by the same O2 source as the machine
It must be routed through the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: The auxiliary O2 flowmeter runs off the same pipeline O2 source, so a pipeline failure or contamination affects it too. It gives up to about 10 L/min to a cannula, mask, or Ambu bag, and it works with the circuit left intact. Automatic shutoff describes the fail-safe acting on other gases. That's why the room setup (MS MAID) includes a resuscitation bag and a separate O2 cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 44 (PDF p. 22); Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Overnight, with the OR empty and the machines off, ambient N2O remains elevated. What is the most likely source?
options: Exhaled gas from the last patient
A loose absorbent canister gasket
A poorly fitting face mask from the last case
A high-pressure leak at an N2O quick connect or cylinder yoke
questions.explanation: When the room isn't in use, background N2O comes mainly from high-pressure leaks (26-750 psig) such as defective quick connects and N2O cylinder yokes. In one OR suite, 50% of machines had major high-pressure leaks. Canister gaskets are low-pressure leaks and only leak while the circuit is pressurized.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 12 (PDF p. 6)

questions.stem: A cylinder won't seat on a yoke with pins in positions 2 and 5. The cylinder's valve has holes at positions 1 and 5. What is happening?
options: An O2 cylinder is being hung on an air yoke, so the yoke pins need replacing
An air cylinder is being hung on an O2 yoke; a second washer will let it seat
An N2O cylinder is being hung on an O2 yoke, and PISS is working
An air cylinder is being hung on an O2 yoke, and PISS is working
questions.explanation: PISS positions: O2 2 and 5, N2O 3 and 5, air 1 and 5. A yoke with pins at 2 and 5 is an O2 yoke, and a valve with holes at 1 and 5 is air, so the pins are correctly blocking a wrong-gas connection. N2O would have holes at 3 and 5. Extra washers can't be used to defeat the system; the lecture's rule is one washer only.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10)

questions.stem: The first-stage pressure regulator reduces cylinder pressure to about 45 psi. Which purposes does the lecture emphasize? Select 2.
options: Preventing damage to anesthesia machine components
Preventing patient barotrauma
Preventing delivery of a hypoxic mixture
Damping pressure to about 14-16 psi for the flowmeters
Proportioning N2O flow to O2 flow
Keeping cylinder pressure above pipeline pressure
questions.explanation: Both are highlighted on slide 24: turning high, variable cylinder pressure into a steady 45 psi protects machine components and prevents barotrauma. Setting it BELOW pipeline pressure keeps the cylinder in reserve. Dropping O2 to about 14-16 psi is the second-stage regulator's job, and hypoxic-mixture protection belongs to the fail-safe and proportioning system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 24 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Compared with the normal loop, the patient's flow-volume loop is most consistent with which condition?
options: COPD
Pulmonary fibrosis
Asthma
Kinked endotracheal tube
questions.explanation: The patient's loop keeps a normal shape but covers a smaller volume, the restrictive pattern: trouble getting air in or expanding, from fibrosis or obesity. Obstructive disease (asthma, COPD, a kinked tube) cuts expiratory flow and produces a scooped expiratory limb at LARGER lung volumes.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 30 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: A CO2 absorber is repacked with granules much smaller than the recommended 4-8 mesh. Which change is MOST likely?
options: More channeling with lower resistance to gas flow
More absorptive surface area with higher resistance to gas flow
Less absorptive surface area with lower resistance to gas flow
Less channeling with lower CO2 absorption efficiency
questions.explanation: Soda lime is sized at 4-8 mesh (a highlighted board topic) to balance surface area against resistance. Smaller granules pack more surface area but leave less gas space, so resistance rises. About half of a normally packed canister is gas. Channeling is flow along the canister walls and through paths in the absorbent; smaller granules don't lower resistance.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 5 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: On a pressure-volume loop, which conditions would require more pressure for the same tidal volume (decreased compliance)? Select 3.
options: Increased inspiratory flow rate
Inadequate muscle relaxation
Pneumothorax
Emphysema
Laparoscopic insufflation
Resolution of a restrictive factor
questions.explanation: Lecture examples of decreased compliance: PE, bronchoconstriction, pneumothorax, laparoscopic insufflation, and inadequate relaxation. Emphysema and resolution of restrictive factors INCREASE compliance. A higher inspiratory flow rate is a resistance-type effect, not a compliance change. The instructor asked you to know what raises and lowers compliance.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 28 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: Which conditions complete the fire triad at an O2 cylinder-to-yoke connection? Select 3.
options: Nitrous oxide acting as the fuel
Room air around the yoke acting as the ignition source
Dust between the tank and yoke acting as fuel
Compressed gas rushing through the outlet generating heat
The Bodok washer acting as the oxidizer
Oxygen acting as the oxidizer
questions.explanation: The triad is oxidizer + fuel + heat. O2 and N2O are both oxidizers, dust between tank and yoke is the fuel, and compressed gas moving through the outlet produces the heat. Calling N2O a fuel is the classic misconception; the washer and room air are misassigned roles.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: During mechanical ventilation, which valve do waste gases leave the breathing circuit through?
options: The ventilator pressure relief valve
The interface's negative-pressure relief valve
The APL valve
The inspiratory unidirectional valve
questions.explanation: With spontaneous or manual ventilation, waste gas exits through the APL (pop-off) valve. When the ventilator is in use, the APL is out of circuit, so waste gas leaves through the ventilator pressure relief valve and travels by conducting tubing to the scavenging interface.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: In the GE Aladin cassette system, desflurane is delivered from an unheated cassette. What makes this possible?
options: The cassette bubbles O2 through liquid agent like a copper kettle
A CPU uses pressure, temperature, and flow sensors to meter agent into the bypass gas
A bimetallic strip inside the cassette adjusts the splitting ratio
The cassette pressurizes desflurane to 2 atm like the Tec 6
questions.explanation: The Aladin CPU identifies each cassette by a magnetic code and uses sensors to run a flow control valve that adds saturated agent to the bypass gas. Instructor note: des isn't heated in this design because the CPU controls the temperature effects. Metal plates and fans under the cassette stabilize temperature.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 66, 67 (PDF p. 33, 34)

questions.stem: A patient rescued from a house fire has an SpO2 of 99% on a standard pulse oximeter but is confused and has a headache. What is the concern?
options: COHb gives a falsely low SpO2; confirm with co-oximetry
SpO2 is accurate because COHb doesn't absorb at 660 or 940 nm
SpO2 is accurate; confirm oxygenation with an ABG PaO2
COHb gives a falsely high SpO2; confirm with co-oximetry
questions.explanation: Carboxyhemoglobin produces falsely HIGH readings; at high COHb levels SpO2 can stay deceptively high despite severely impaired tissue oxygenation. Two-wavelength oximetry can't tell COHb from oxyhemoglobin; lab co-oximeters use multiple wavelengths to measure it. A PaO2 only shows dissolved O2, so it can look normal.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 74, 75, 76 (PDF p. 75, 76, 77)

questions.stem: An obese patient's BP is taken with a standard adult cuff whose bladder covers well under 80% of the arm. It reads 172/96. How should you interpret this?
options: Accurate, because oscillometric MAP isn't affected by cuff size
Likely falsely high; move the cuff to the forearm to confirm
Likely falsely high; replace it with a correctly sized cuff
Likely falsely low; the cuff under-compresses the artery
questions.explanation: A cuff that is too small (or loose) gives falsely HIGH readings; too large gives falsely low. Obesity increases arm circumference, so cuff choice matters. Moving to the forearm isn't a fix, because forearm measurements can overestimate BP.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 62, 90 (PDF p. 63, 91)

questions.stem: Which tube best suits prone surgery with the neck sharply flexed, where kinking is the main concern?
options: Standard PVC tube
Armored (anode) tube
Nasal RAE tube
Oral RAE tube
questions.explanation: Armored (anode or flexo-metallic) tubes have a spiral wire embedded in the shaft that resists kinking and compression, which suits head, neck, and tracheal surgery. RAE tubes have a preformed bend to route the connector away from the surgical field (oromaxillofacial and nasal procedures).
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: Right after intubation, an asthmatic patient's capnogram shows a slow, rounded upstroke that never forms a flat plateau. PIP rises while plateau pressure is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Circuit leak
Decreased compliance from chest wall rigidity
Bronchospasm
Exhausted CO2 absorbent
questions.explanation: A slow B-to-C rise that rounds off into a shark fin is the obstructive pattern. Instructor note: the more C rounds out, the more obstruction. Combined with isolated PIP elevation (a resistance problem), this is bronchospasm. An exhausted absorbent raises the baseline, and chest wall rigidity would raise plateau too.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 45, 46, 51 (PDF p. 46, 47, 52)

questions.stem: Where is the O2 fail-safe valve located, and what does it sense?
options: In the N2O supply line; it senses O2 supply pressure
In the N2O supply line; it senses inspired O2 concentration
In the O2 supply line; it senses N2O supply pressure
In the O2 supply line; it senses O2 flow at the flowmeter
questions.explanation: Instructor note: it sits in the nitrous line but responds to O2 pressure. When O2 supply pressure falls below about 25-30 psig it reduces, and below about 20 psig stops, the flow of other gases. It never measures concentration, so it can't catch the wrong gas in the O2 line.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 34 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: Core temperature is 36.0 C and mean skin temperature is 32.0 C. Using the lecture's formula, what is the mean body temperature?
questions.explanation: Mean body temperature = 0.85 x core + 0.15 x skin = 30.6 + 4.8 = 35.4 C. 34.0 is a simple average, which overweights skin. This is why skin temperature alone doesn't represent mean body temperature and core sites are preferred.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 81 (PDF p. 82)

questions.stem: In a cannot intubate, cannot ventilate situation, cricothyrotomy goes through a membrane bounded by which structures?
options: Inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and superior edge of the cricoid
The epiglottis and the arytenoid cartilages
Superior border of the thyroid cartilage and the hyoid bone
Inferior edge of the cricoid cartilage and the first tracheal ring
questions.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane is a fibroelastic membrane attached to the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and the superior edge of the cricoid cartilage. Cricothyrotomy (needle, percutaneous, or surgical) is the final option in every CICO algorithm.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 15 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: Why is the CO2 absorber almost always placed in the inspiratory limb, on the bag side of the circle system?
options: So its resistance can be overcome by assisted or controlled ventilation
So the APL valve vents only CO2-free gas
So it sits downstream of the fresh gas inlet
So exhaled gas is scrubbed before it reaches the reservoir bag
questions.explanation: The absorber can sit in any of the four quadrants, but it is placed in the inspiratory limb on the bag side so the resistance it adds can be overcome by assisted or controlled ventilation. The other choices describe placement rationales the lecture doesn't give. The absorber is required for low-flow technique and also conserves heat and humidity.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Which are consequences of perioperative hypothermia? Select 3.
options: Impaired coagulation
Reduced cardiac work
Increased O2 consumption from shivering
Improved platelet function
Faster drug metabolism
Increased wound infection
questions.explanation: Hypothermia increases shivering, cardiac work, and O2 consumption; impairs coagulation; alters (slows) drug metabolism; and is linked to myocardial ischemia and wound infection. Each wrong choice is the opposite direction. Instructor note: low temp is bad for coagulation, wounds, and drug function.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 84 (PDF p. 85)

questions.stem: N2O is used as the sole anesthetic agent. Per NIOSH, what is the maximum time-weighted average exposure for OR personnel?
options: 2 ppm
25 ppm
50 ppm
100 ppm
questions.explanation: NIOSH: halogenated agents used alone, no more than 2 ppm; N2O as the sole agent, no more than 25 ppm TWA during administration. There's no universal WAG standard, and OSHA recommends scavenging in all anesthetizing locations.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)
questions.supp: NIOSH's 1977 recommendation also covers combined use: when halogenated agents are given WITH N2O, the halogenated limit drops from 2 ppm to 0.5 ppm (ceiling over a sampling period up to 1 hour), and N2O stays at 25 ppm TWA. Slide 10 lists only the 2 ppm and 25 ppm values.

questions.stem: Late in a long high-flow case, the liquid sevo in a variable bypass vaporizer cools. How does the temperature compensation valve respond?
options: Bends to send more fresh gas through the vaporizing chamber
Activates a heater to rewarm the sump to 39 C
Bends to send more fresh gas through the bypass
Holds the splitting ratio fixed at whatever the dial sets
questions.explanation: Vaporization cools the liquid, and vapor pressure falls with temperature. To keep output constant, the bimetallic strip bends as temperature drops to increase flow through the sump, changing the splitting ratio. More bypass flow would lower output further. Heating to 39 C belongs to the desflurane Tec 6.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 56 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: Immediately after intubation, this capnogram appears and shrinks over several breaths. What is the best interpretation and response?
options: Tracheal placement with hypoventilation; increase minute ventilation
Tracheal placement, since CO2 was detected on the first breaths
A kinked sampling line; replace it and continue
Esophageal placement; remove the tube and reestablish ventilation
questions.explanation: Low, fading CO2 waves that don't form a plateau are the esophageal pattern shown in the lecture; the tracheal trace is square and stable. Confirmation needs 3 full consecutive ETCO2 waveforms plus bilateral breath sounds and chest expansion. Instructor note: failure to recognize misplacement is catastrophic.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 92, 93 (PDF p. 93, 94)

questions.stem: At high flow rates, the annular space around a flowmeter float behaves like an orifice. Flow through it then depends mainly on the gas's:
options: Density, because flow becomes laminar
Density, because flow becomes turbulent
Viscosity, because flow becomes turbulent
Viscosity, because flow becomes laminar
questions.explanation: At low flows the annular space is longer than it is wide (tube shaped), flow is laminar, and viscosity governs it. At high flows it is wider than long (orifice shaped), flow is turbulent, and density governs it. The distractors mix up the pairings.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 43 (PDF p. 22)

questions.stem: A donated cylinder painted solid white under the international color code arrives on a mission trip. Which gas does it contain?
options: Nitrogen
Nitrous oxide
Oxygen
Medical air
questions.explanation: International coding on the lecture table: O2 white, air white and black, N2O blue, N2 black. In the US, O2 is green and air is yellow. Solid white means O2 internationally; air is the two-tone cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Which features are characteristic of the desflurane-specific (Tec 6) vaporizer? Select 3.
options: The sump is heated to 39 C
The dial controls a restrictor valve in the vapor circuit
A bimetallic strip provides temperature compensation
Wicks and baffles saturate the carrier gas
It works without electrical power
Liquid desflurane is pressurized to about 2 atm
questions.explanation: The Tec 6 heats the sump to 39 C and pressurizes des to 2 atm (about 1500 mmHg). Restrictor #1 is a shut-off that opens once warm; restrictor #2 is set by the dial. A differential pressure transducer balances the gas and vapor circuits. Wicks, baffles, and a bimetallic strip are variable bypass features, and the des vaporizer requires electricity.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 60, 61, 62, 63 (PDF p. 30, 31, 32)

questions.stem: A patient emerging in PACU has partial upper airway obstruction and gags when an oral airway is attempted. Which device is the better choice?
options: Larger oropharyngeal airway
Laryngeal mask airway
Nasopharyngeal airway
Smaller oropharyngeal airway
questions.explanation: Awake patients tolerate NPAs better than OPAs. Any OPA, larger or smaller, can stimulate oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes in a lightly anesthetized patient, and an LMA won't be tolerated either. Insert the NPA with water-based lubricant or local anesthetic; its most common complication is epistaxis.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 5, 6 (PDF p. 5, 6)

questions.stem: A ventilated patient in the sitting position suddenly becomes hypotensive. ETCO2 falls sharply and end-tidal nitrogen appears, while PIP and exhaled volume are unchanged. What is most likely?
options: Circuit disconnection
Vaporizer malfunction
Venous air embolism
Endotracheal cuff leak
questions.explanation: The lecture's analyzer table lists air embolism as a CO2 plus N2 event. A cuff leak also shows N2 and CO2, but it lowers exhaled volume and doesn't cause sudden hypotension. A disconnection would drop pressure and volume, and a vaporizer problem only changes the agent reading.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 42 (PDF p. 42)

questions.stem: An O2 E-cylinder gauge reads 950 psig. A patient needs 5 L/min by face mask during transport. About how long will the cylinder last?
options: About 33 minutes
About 66 minutes
About 132 minutes
About 190 minutes
questions.explanation: O2 is a compressed gas, so contents fall in proportion to pressure. A full cylinder is about 1900 psig and 660 L, so 950 psig is about half full, roughly 330 L. 330 L divided by 5 L/min is about 66 minutes. 132 minutes comes from using the full 660 L and forgetting the tank is half empty.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which factors degrade the dynamic fidelity of an arterial pressure monitoring system? Select 3.
options: Zeroing and leveling at the right atrium
Excess tubing length and stopcocks
Short, noncompliant tubing
Clot at the catheter tip
Air bubbles in the tubing
A continuous flush of about 3 mL/hr
questions.explanation: Air bubbles, excessive tubing, stopcocks, clot, and catheter kinking all degrade fidelity. The lecture advises keeping tubing length, connections, and stopcocks to a minimum. Zeroing and leveling to the right atrium is correct practice, and a 3-6 mL/hr continuous flush is normal (though that volume matters in neonates).
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 69 (PDF p. 70)

questions.stem: Which factors promote compound A production from sevoflurane? Select 3.
options: Using desflurane instead of sevoflurane
Moister absorbent
Higher sevoflurane concentration
Drier absorbent
Higher fresh gas flow
Warmer absorbent
questions.explanation: Compound A is promoted by warmer, drier absorbent, higher agent concentration, and LOWER fresh gas flow. Water in the absorbent helps break compound A down into low-toxicity products. Desflurane's problem is CO, not compound A.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 6 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Before the first case, an SRNA has checked the machine, placed monitors, opened airway equipment, primed IV lines, and drawn up drugs. Using MS MAID, what was missed?
options: Spare O2 cylinder
Backup airway equipment
Suction
Nerve stimulator
questions.explanation: MS MAID = Machine, Suction, Monitors, Airway, IV, Drugs. Suction (canister, tubing, Yankauer, on, working, in reach) is the step left out, and it's highlighted on the slide. A spare O2 cylinder belongs to the machine check, a nerve stimulator to monitors, and backup airway gear to airway.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Each diagram shows a leak in one flowmeter tube; arrows show where gas travels. Which arrangements could deliver a hypoxic mixture to the outlet? Select 2.
options: Diagram A
Diagram B
Diagram C
Diagram D
None, because the fail-safe valve senses flowmeter leaks
All four, because O2 position doesn't affect leak behavior
questions.explanation: In A and B, O2 enters upstream of the leaking tube, so O2 escapes through the leak while N2O continues to the outlet. In C (Drager) and D (Ohmeda), O2 is the last flowmeter, closest to the outlet, so an upstream leak loses N2O or air instead of O2. Instructor note: oxygen is always last. The fail-safe responds only to O2 supply pressure and can't detect a low-pressure leak.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 41 (PDF p. 21)

questions.stem: Arterial pressure is 150/60 mmHg. What are the calculated MAP and pulse pressure?
options: MAP 105, pulse pressure 90
MAP 80, pulse pressure 90
MAP 90, pulse pressure 60
MAP 90, pulse pressure 90
questions.explanation: MAP = (SBP + 2 x DBP) / 3 = (150 + 120) / 3 = 90. Pulse pressure (highlighted on the slide) = SBP minus DBP = 90. 105 is the simple average of systolic and diastolic, which ignores that diastole takes up more of the cycle.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 64 (PDF p. 65)

questions.stem: On an arterial waveform, which feature marks closure of the aortic valve and the start of diastole?
options: Systolic peak
Dicrotic notch
Systolic upstroke
Diastolic runoff
questions.explanation: The dicrotic notch is the small dip on the downslope marking aortic valve closure. The systolic upstroke follows aortic valve opening, its peak is SBP, and diastolic runoff ends at the lowest point, DBP. MAP is the area under the curve. Instructor note: know the A-line parts.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 72 (PDF p. 73)

questions.stem: What defines the sniffing position?
options: Fully extending the cervical spine with the occiput flat on the bed
Elevating the occiput and extending the head at the atlanto-occipital joint
Flexing the neck while keeping the head neutral
Extending the lower cervical spine with the occiput flat on the bed
questions.explanation: Sniffing position = elevation of the occiput plus extension of the head at the atlanto-occipital joint. Extension alone, or extension in the wrong place with the occiput flat, misses the occiput elevation.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: The OR table is raised 15 cm, but the arterial transducer stays on the IV pole at its original height. What happens to the displayed pressure?
options: Falsely high, because the transducer is now below the heart
Unchanged, because the system was zeroed at the start
Falsely low, because the transducer is now below the heart
Falsely high for systolic pressure only
questions.explanation: The transducer must be leveled to the reference point, usually the right atrium. Because of gravity, the level of the transducer relative to the heart changes the reading. A transducer below the heart carries the extra fluid column and reads falsely high. Before treating a sudden change, verify leveling, tubing, catheter patency, and waveform fidelity.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 66, 70 (PDF p. 67, 71)

questions.stem: Which agents do not produce carbon monoxide in the presence of CO2 absorbents? Select 2.
options: Desflurane
Any agent containing an -O-CHF2 group
Isoflurane
Enflurane
Halothane
Sevoflurane
questions.explanation: CO comes from the difluoromethyl ethers, which contain an -O-CHF2 group: desflurane (most), enflurane, then isoflurane. Sevoflurane and halothane lack that group. Sevo's problem with dry absorbent is compound A instead.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: In which situations may ETCO2 significantly underestimate PaCO2? Select 3.
options: Fever
Bicarbonate administration
Pulmonary embolism
Low cardiac output
Hypoventilation
One-lung ventilation
questions.explanation: ETCO2 underestimates PaCO2 when dead space or V/Q mismatch rises: PE, emphysema, one-lung ventilation, low cardiac output, or an adult circuit on a child. Hypoventilation, fever, and bicarbonate raise CO2 but don't widen the gradient themselves.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 49 (PDF p. 50)

questions.stem: During a spontaneously breathing LMA case, the analyzer shows expired nitrogen and a lower ETCO2. Hemodynamics are stable and SpO2 is 99%. The pattern best fits:
options: Poor LMA fit entraining room air
Vaporizer contamination
Malignant hyperthermia
Circuit hypoxia
questions.explanation: The lecture's analyzer table lists poor mask or LMA fit as an N2 plus CO2 event: room air enters around the device and dilutes the expired CO2. MH raises CO2, vaporizer problems show up in agent analysis, and circuit hypoxia shows up in O2 analysis. Instructor tip: one gas changing points to the patient; all gases changing points to equipment.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 42 (PDF p. 42)

questions.stem: Power to a Tec 6 desflurane vaporizer is lost mid-case. What should you expect?
options: Output continues at the dialed setting using stored heat
Vapor output stops, because the vaporizer depends on electricity
The unit converts to variable bypass operation
Output surges because the pressure regulator fails open
questions.explanation: The Tec 6 heats and pressurizes the sump and balances its circuits electronically; the lecture flags that it requires electricity. Its vapor circuit shut-off (restrictor #1) opens only when the unit is warm and the dial is on, so without power, vapor delivery stops. Expired agent monitoring will show the fall.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 62, 65 (PDF p. 31, 33)

questions.stem: About 5 mL of liquid isoflurane spills while a vaporizer is being refilled. Roughly how much vapor is added to the room air?
options: About 200 mL
About 500 mL
About 1,000 mL
About 5,000 mL
questions.explanation: Each mL of spilled liquid agent adds about 200 mL of vapor, the same 1 mL to 200 mL figure used for vaporizer consumption. 5 mL x 200 mL = about 1,000 mL.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: Where should the O2 analyzer sensor be placed, and why?
options: Y-piece, to estimate arterial oxygenation
Expiratory limb, to detect circuit disconnection
Common gas outlet, to detect flowmeter leaks
Inspiratory limb, to detect delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture
questions.explanation: The sensor goes in the inspired limb to catch hypoxic gas delivery. Inspired O2 alarms don't reliably detect circuit disconnection, and adequate FiO2 doesn't guarantee adequate PaO2 or tissue oxygenation.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 36, 38 (PDF p. 36, 38)

questions.stem: Which causes raise peak inspiratory pressure while plateau pressure stays essentially unchanged? Select 3.
options: Tension pneumothorax
Ascites
Kinked endotracheal tube
Endobronchial intubation
Airway secretions
Endotracheal tube cuff herniation
questions.explanation: From the lecture's list, increased PIP with unchanged plateau comes from higher inspiratory flow or higher airway resistance: kinked tube, bronchospasm, secretions, foreign body, airway compression, cuff herniation. Tension pneumothorax, ascites, and endobronchial intubation lower compliance and raise both. A suction catheter quickly rules out secretions or kinking.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 32 (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: When ramping an obese patient for induction, what is the positioning target?
options: Chin level with the xiphoid process
Occiput flat on the bed with the shoulders elevated
Head flat with a roll under the shoulders
External ear canal level with the sternal notch
questions.explanation: The ramped position stacks blankets under the upper back and head until the ear lines up horizontally with the sternal notch, with head elevation. This improves the laryngoscopic view in obese patients.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Which conditions worsen the pumping effect in a variable bypass vaporizer? Select 3.
options: Positive pressure ventilation
Low fresh gas flow
A completely full vaporizer
Low level of liquid agent
High fresh gas flow
An outlet check valve between vaporizer and common gas outlet
questions.explanation: Pumping is retrograde pressure from the circuit pushed back into the vaporizer during PPV or O2 flush use. It is worse with low FGF and a low liquid level, contaminates the bypass channel, and raises the delivered concentration. A check valve between the vaporizer and common gas outlet minimizes it.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 72 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: During femoral cementing for a hip arthroplasty, ETCO2 abruptly falls from 36 to 18 mmHg with a preserved waveform shape, and BP drops. What is the most likely cause?
options: Hypoventilation
Sampling line disconnection
Malignant hyperthermia
Pulmonary embolism
questions.explanation: A sudden drop in ETCO2 with hypotension fits decreased CO2 delivery to the lungs: massive PE, low cardiac output, or hypotension (Box 18.1 and slide 50). A sampling line disconnection would wipe out the waveform, and hypoventilation and MH RAISE ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 43, 50 (PDF p. 43, 51)

questions.stem: A canister holds 1,000 g of soda lime. Roughly how much CO2 can it absorb before it is exhausted?
options: About 26 L
About 190 L
About 260 L
About 800 L
questions.explanation: Soda lime absorbs 19% of its weight in CO2, which the lecture translates to about 26 L per 100 g. 1,000 g x 26 L per 100 g is about 260 L. 190 L comes from treating the 19% figure as liters.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 2 (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Which statements about pipeline wall connections are accurate? Select 3.
options: Quick connectors are gas specific but not standardized across manufacturers
PISS is the indexing system used at pipeline wall outlets
Central vacuum outlets are coded purple
Quick connectors are the nationally standardized terminal fitting
Waste anesthetic gas disposal outlets are coded purple
DISS uses a nationally standardized thread with gas-specific diameters
questions.explanation: DISS gives each gas a unique diameter on a standardized thread. Quick connectors allow fast connection but are manufacturer specific with no standardization. Waste gas is purple and central vacuum is white. PISS is the cylinder-to-yoke system, not the wall outlet system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 29, 30 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: Which practices does the lecture recommend to reduce the environmental impact of inhaled anesthetics? Select 2.
options: Use N2O routinely for labor analgesia because it is short-lived
Prefer desflurane for short cases because it has the shortest atmospheric life
Raise fresh gas flow at emergence to limit total agent use
Choose isoflurane over sevoflurane for its shorter atmospheric life
Avoid unnecessarily high fresh gas flows, especially with desflurane
Avoid N2O as a carrier gas
questions.explanation: Atmospheric lifetimes: sevo 1.1 yr, iso 3.2 yr, des 14 yr, N2O up to 114 yr. So des and N2O are the worst offenders. The lecture recommends avoiding N2O as a carrier gas, avoiding high FGF (especially with des), and reconsidering N2O for routine labor analgesia.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 22, 23 (PDF p. 11, 12)

questions.stem: A patient receives deep sedation for colonoscopy with no airway device. What does the ASA standard require for ventilation monitoring?
options: Continual observation of clinical signs only
Continuous exhaled CO2 only if supplemental O2 is given
Pulse oximetry alone, since no airway device is placed
Continual clinical signs plus continuous exhaled CO2 monitoring
questions.explanation: For moderate to deep sedation, ventilation is evaluated by continual observation of clinical signs AND continuous exhaled CO2. Clinical signs alone are acceptable only for local or regional anesthesia with minimal or no sedation. Capnography is required during moderate or deep sedation (slide 47).
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 94 (PDF p. 95)

questions.stem: Downstream of the second-stage regulator, what pressure reaches the O2 flow control valve?
options: About 45 psi
About 14-16 psi
About 26-38 psi
About 50-55 psi
questions.explanation: Second-stage regulators drop pipeline or cylinder pressure further and damp fluctuations: about 14-16 psi for O2 and 26-38 psi for N2O. 45 psi is the first-stage (cylinder) output and 50-55 psi is pipeline pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: For a laser airway procedure, which measures reduce the risk of an airway fire? Select 2.
options: Fill the cuff with saline or water and dye
Use N2O as the carrier gas to lower the O2 concentration
Use an ETT made of noncombustible, laser-resistant material
Increase FiO2 to maximize oxygen reserve
Fill the cuff with air so a rupture is easier to detect
Use a standard PVC tube with a well-inflated cuff
questions.explanation: Airway fire is the most serious laser hazard. Ignition depends on tube material, O2 or N2O concentration, and direct heat contact. PVC tubes are flammable, so use a laser-resistant tube. The cuff itself isn't laser resistant, so fill it with saline or water and dye. N2O supports combustion just like O2.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: Two O2 cylinders hang on a double yoke. Cylinder A is open; empty cylinder B has just been removed. Why doesn't O2 from A vent out of yoke B?
options: System pressure pushes the yoke B check valve into its seated position
The PISS pins seal yoke B once the cylinder is removed
The first-stage regulator closes when yoke B is empty
The fail-safe valve closes the yoke B pathway
questions.explanation: Each yoke has a one-way check valve. Gas pressure in the system pushes the valve in the empty yoke backward into its seated (closed) position, which prevents gas loss and transfilling from a full cylinder into an empty one. Instructor note: the yoke B check valve keeps gas from A from escaping or filling B.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 22 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: In Landesberg's vascular surgery study, which lead detected perioperative ischemia earliest and most often?
options: V4
V5
Lead II
V3
questions.explanation: V3 was most sensitive (86.8%), V4 second (78.9%), and V5 third (65.8%). 97% of ischemic events showed ST depression, not elevation. Instructor note: monitor lead II for rhythm and V3 for ischemia. V5 is the classic trap answer.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 58 (PDF p. 59)

questions.stem: Which items are part of USDOT cylinder markings? Select 3.
options: Serial number
Volume of gas remaining
Date the cylinder was last filled
Expiration date of the gas
Tare (empty) weight
Rated filling pressure
questions.explanation: USDOT markings include the regulating agency, cylinder metal, rated filling pressure, tare weight, serial number, manufacture date and manufacturer, owner (neck ring), retest markings (star), and gas hazards. Nothing stamped on the cylinder tells you remaining volume (that comes from the gauge, or weight for N2O), and fill or expiration dates aren't among the listed markings.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 9 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: Minutes after CO2 insufflation for laparoscopy, ETCO2 rises from 35 to 44 mmHg with a normal waveform shape and unchanged ventilator settings. What is the most likely cause?
options: A sampling line leak
Bronchospasm from abdominal distention
Increased CO2 delivery from absorbed insufflated CO2
Exhausted CO2 absorbent
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists laparoscopic surgery under increased CO2 delivery or production. A normal waveform shape argues against bronchospasm (shark fin) and against an exhausted absorbent (elevated baseline). Instructor note: insufflating the abdomen also mimics a restrictive pattern on the loops.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 43, 46 (PDF p. 43, 47)

questions.stem: How does an electronic flow control valve differ from a mechanical one?
options: It changes orifice size through a hand-turned needle
It keeps working without electricity during a power failure
It uses pressure sensors and feedback for more precise control
It senses O2 concentration rather than pressure or flow
questions.explanation: Mechanical valves are adjusted by the flowmeter knob, which changes the orifice size. Electronic valves are integrated into the machine and use pressure sensors and feedback from gas monitors for more precise control, so they depend on power. Neither type measures O2 concentration directly.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 35 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: Per the instructor's notes, which airway device more commonly vents excess anesthetic gas into the room?
options: Double-lumen tube
Laryngeal mask airway
Cuffed endotracheal tube
Armored endotracheal tube
questions.explanation: A poorly fitting face mask, LMA, or other airway device lets gas leak around the rim, and the instructor noted LMAs more commonly vent excess gas. A properly sized, well-seated cuffed tube limits leakage. The lecture also flags being mindful of pregnant providers and staff.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: After an ETT or supraglottic airway is placed, which does the ASA standard require? Select 3.
options: An ETCO2 alarm audible to the anesthesia team
A disconnect alarm only if volume alarms are turned off
ETCO2 monitoring only for ETTs, not supraglottic airways
A qualitative color-change detector as the continual monitor
Continual quantitative ETCO2 until removal or transfer to recovery
Verifying placement by clinical assessment and by CO2 in the expired gas
questions.explanation: ASA requires verifying ETT or SGA position by clinical assessment and expired CO2; continual ETCO2 by a quantitative method (capnography, capnometry, mass spectroscopy) until removal or transfer; and an audible ETCO2 alarm. With mechanical ventilation, a disconnect device with an audible alarm must be in continuous use.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 92 (PDF p. 93)

questions.stem: The patient's flow-volume loop is shown beside a normal reference. Which disease pattern does it fit?
options: Obesity
Pulmonary fibrosis
COPD
A normal variant
questions.explanation: The patient's expiratory flow is reduced and the expiratory limb is scooped, while volume stays large: the obstructive pattern (trouble getting air out) seen in COPD and asthma. Fibrosis and obesity are restrictive, with a normal shape at smaller volumes.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 30 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: A technician lists machine parts that operate between the first-stage regulator and the flow control valves. Which two belong on that list? Select 2.
options: Common gas outlet
Flowmeter float
Hanger yoke
O2 flush valve
Vaporizer
Pipeline inlet connection
questions.explanation: The intermediate system runs from the first-stage regulator (and pipeline inlets) to the flow control valves. It includes pipeline inlets, second-stage regulators, the fail-safe, flow control, and flush valves, and indicators and alarms. Instructor note: the flush is the last part of the intermediate system. The hanger yoke is high pressure; flowmeters, vaporizers, and the common gas outlet are low pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 26, 36 (PDF p. 13, 18)

questions.stem: In soda lime, sodium carbonate reacts with which compound to regenerate sodium hydroxide?
options: Calcium hydroxide, forming calcium carbonate
Potassium hydroxide, forming potassium carbonate
Water, forming carbonic acid
