questions.stem: Over 90 minutes, ETCO2 creeps up and inspired CO2 rises to 4 mmHg. Vitals and ventilator settings are unchanged, and the absorbent shows little color change. What is the best action?
options: Raise minute ventilation and recheck in 30 minutes
Change the absorbent; color change isn't reliable
Lower fresh gas flow to reduce the CO2 load
Keep the absorbent, since it hasn't changed color
questions.explanation: Instructor note: EtCO2 creeping up without any other problems points to the absorbent. Rising inspired CO2 means rebreathing. The highlighted slide point is that indicator color is not to be relied on (regeneration, channeling, bleaching). Lowering FGF increases rebreathing and uses absorbent faster.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 2, 4 (PDF p. 1, 2)

questions.stem: Which scavenging-system problems can spill waste gas into the OR? Select 3.
options: The pop-in valve admitting room air during high suction
A dedicated evacuation system instead of wall suction
Inadequate vacuum or ventilation flow overloading the system
Leaking rubber parts or relief valves in the scavenger
Nonrecirculating OR ventilation used for disposal
Improperly sized scavenger hoses
questions.explanation: Slide 13: the scavenging system itself can leak through rubber parts and safety valves or improperly sized hoses, and it can be overloaded by inadequate vacuum or ventilation, spilling waste gas into the room. The pop-in valve pulls room air IN. Dedicated evacuation (preferred) and nonrecirculating ventilation are proper disposal routes.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: The O2 pipeline has failed and the O2 cylinder is still closed. What happens when the O2 flush is pressed?
options: Normal flush flow supplied from the N2O line
35-75 L/min from reserve stored in the second-stage regulator
Little or no flow, because the flush draws from the pipeline or first-stage regulator
Normal flush flow supplied through the auxiliary O2 flowmeter
questions.explanation: The flush opens O2 flow from the pipeline or the first-stage (cylinder) regulator straight to the common gas outlet. With the pipeline failed and the cylinder closed, it has no O2 source. Open the cylinder first.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 36 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: Shortly after an IV dye is injected, SpO2 abruptly drops from 99% to 88% while ETCO2, BP, and the patient's color are unchanged. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: True desaturation from a new intrapulmonary shunt
Motion artifact from the arm during injection
Dye interference with the oximeter's light absorption
Methemoglobinemia caused by the injected dye
questions.explanation: The lecture lists dyes among factors that impair pulse oximetry, along with motion, low perfusion, hypothermia, nail polish, and ambient light. An abrupt drop right after injection with every other sign unchanged points to artifact. Still assess the patient, per the cognitive-bias lesson on alarms.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 78 (PDF p. 79)

questions.stem: Which O2 analyzer types generate an electrical current proportional to O2? Select 2.
options: Paramagnetic analyzer
Thermistor probe
Two-wavelength pulse oximeter
Polarographic electrode
Galvanic cell
Infrared absorption analyzer
questions.explanation: Galvanic cells generate current from an O2-dependent chemical reaction, and polarographic sensors measure current as O2 diffuses through a membrane and is reduced (O2 + 2H2O + 4e- -> 4OH-). Paramagnetic analyzers detect a pressure change from O2's attraction to switched magnetic fields; infrared measures CO2, N2O, and agents.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 35 (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: During a GA case, the O2 analyzer's low-concentration alarm has been disabled. Which ASA standard does this violate?
options: Standard I, personnel
Standard 2.1, oxygenation
Standard 2.2, ventilation
Standard 2.3, circulation
questions.explanation: ASA 2.1 requires that during every GA using an anesthesia machine, circuit O2 concentration be measured by an analyzer with a low O2 concentration limit alarm in use. Ventilation (2.2) covers ETCO2 and clinical signs.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 11 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: During one-handed mask ventilation, a leak persists along the jaw. Which hand position does the lecture describe for a tight seal?
options: Three fingers on the mask body and two under the chin soft tissue
All five fingers spread over the mask body
Two fingers on the mask and three pressing the submandibular soft tissue
Two fingers on the mask body and three along the bony mandible
questions.explanation: Two fingers go over the body of the mask and three fingers along the BONY mandible to complete the seal. The lecture specifies the bony mandible, not soft tissue, for the three-finger grip.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Two oscillometric monitors on the same patient show identical MAPs but different systolic and diastolic values. Why?
options: Systolic and diastolic are measured directly while MAP is calculated
Each monitor measures a different artery's MAP
One monitor uses Korotkoff sounds for MAP
MAP comes from maximal oscillation; SBP and DBP are estimated by device-specific algorithms
questions.explanation: Oscillometric devices detect pulsations in the cuff. MAP is associated with the maximal oscillation amplitude, while systolic and diastolic values are estimated using device-specific algorithms, which is why readings vary between devices.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 86 (PDF p. 87)

questions.stem: A spontaneously breathing LMA patient has RR 28, ETCO2 28 mmHg with a normal waveform, and rising HR and BP after incision. What is the most likely cause?
options: Poor LMA fit entraining room air
Pulmonary embolism reducing CO2 delivery
Hyperventilation from pain or light anesthesia
Decreased CO2 production from hypothermia
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists pain, anxiety, and awareness or 'light' anesthesia under hyperventilation causing decreased ETCO2. Rapid breathing with tachycardia and hypertension after stimulation fits. PE would drop BP, and an LMA leak shows up as expired N2 with a distorted trace.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 43 (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: How does fresh gas pick up agent in a Tec 6 desflurane vaporizer, compared with a variable bypass vaporizer?
options: Part of the fresh gas passes through the sump and is saturated
Fresh gas is bubbled through liquid des like a copper kettle
All fresh gas flows over wicks soaked with heated des
Fresh gas never enters the sump; pure des vapor is injected into it
questions.explanation: The Tec 6 runs two parallel circuits. Fresh gas flows through the gas circuit restrictor, while the heated, pressurized sump supplies 100% des vapor through restrictor valves into that gas stream. A variable bypass vaporizer instead splits fresh gas and saturates the portion that passes through the chamber.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 61, 62 (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: Without scavenging, room N2O measures 200 ppm. About what level would a properly functioning scavenging system be expected to produce?
options: About 2 ppm
About 20 ppm
About 100 ppm
About 180 ppm
questions.explanation: A properly functioning scavenging system reduces trace WAG concentrations by about 90%, so 200 ppm falls to about 20 ppm. That's still close to NIOSH's 25 ppm N2O limit, which is why technique errors (the source of 94-99% of contamination) still matter.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 18 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: The first GA case follows a sedation case that used a Mapleson circuit. After induction, the circle bag won't fill even though flowmeters show 2 L/min. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The O2 fail-safe valve has closed
The proportioning system is limiting O2 flow
The auxiliary common gas outlet is still diverting fresh gas
The vaporizer interlock is blocking flow to the circle
questions.explanation: The auxiliary common gas outlet diverts fresh gas flow to a separate circuit such as a Mapleson, cannula, or mask. Left in that position, the flowmeters register flow but none reaches the circle. The fail-safe and proportioner respond to O2 pressure and ratios, not outlet selection.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 75 (PDF p. 38)

questions.stem: Why does the pumping effect raise delivered concentration from a variable bypass vaporizer?
options: Back pressure closes the temperature compensation valve
Back pressure forces liquid agent into the fresh gas outlet
Retrograde pressure cools the liquid and raises vapor pressure
Retrograde pressure pushes vapor-saturated gas back into the bypass channel
questions.explanation: PPV or O2 flush transmits pressure back into the vaporizer. When pressure releases, saturated gas from the chamber expands into the bypass channel, so the outflow carries extra agent. It's worse at low FGF and low liquid levels, and an outlet check valve minimizes it.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 72 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: About 100 g of water evaporates from an open abdomen during a case. Using the lecture's figure, how much heat is removed?
options: About 5.8 kcal
About 58 kcal
About 580 kcal
About 0.58 kcal
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes about 0.58 kcal of heat for every gram of water vaporized: 100 g x 0.58 = 58 kcal. Radiation is still the largest source of heat loss overall.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 80 (PDF p. 81)

questions.stem: A sedated patient breathing supplemental O2 becomes apneic. Which monitor will reveal the problem first?
options: Capnography
Pulse oximetry
Expired anesthetic agent analysis
Inspired O2 analyzer
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry is a poor indicator of ventilation: a patient on supplemental O2 may be apneic for several minutes before desaturation shows up. Capnography shows loss of expired CO2 with the next missed breath. The inspired O2 analyzer measures delivered gas, and agent analysis is irrelevant without a volatile.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 41, 78 (PDF p. 41, 79)

questions.stem: When estimating surgical blood loss, which sources should be counted? Select 3.
options: Laparotomy pads and sponges
OG tube drainage
Suction canister volume after subtracting irrigation
Blood on the floor and drapes
Total suction canister volume including irrigation
Urine output
questions.explanation: Slide 55 lists laps, sponges, suction, and the floor as blood loss sources. Irrigation in the canister must be subtracted, or loss is overestimated. Urine and gastric output are fluid losses, not blood loss. Instructor note: know roughly the amount of blood loss and where you are in the case timeline.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 55 (PDF p. 56)

questions.stem: During a long case, the N2O E-cylinder gauge begins falling from 745 psig and now reads 400 psig. What does this mean?
options: Contents are unchanged; N2O pressure never reflects volume
About half the N2O remains, since 400 is about half of 745 psig
The liquid is gone; remaining gas now falls with pressure, about 215 L at 400 psig
Liquid remains; the drop reflects a failing first-stage regulator
questions.explanation: N2O holds at 745 psig while liquid and gas are in equilibrium. Once the last liquid vaporizes, only gas remains and pressure falls in proportion to volume. The lecture's figure shows about 215 L left at 400 psig, so the cylinder is nearly empty. The 'half full' reasoning applies the O2 rule to the liquid phase, which doesn't work.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: During CPR on an intubated patient, ETCO2 reads 6 mmHg with a consistent waveform. What does the lecture recommend?
options: Improve compression quality to keep ETCO2 at least 10 mmHg
Remove the tube, since ETCO2 under 10 means esophageal placement
Increase ventilation rate to raise ETCO2 above 10
Accept it, since any detectable CO2 confirms adequate CPR
questions.explanation: CPR assessment on slide 46: attempt to maintain a minimum ETCO2 of 10 mmHg, which reflects the pulmonary blood flow that compressions generate. A consistent waveform supports tracheal placement. Faster ventilation LOWERS ETCO2 instead of raising it.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 46 (PDF p. 47)

questions.stem: During a machine check, one of the two index pins on the O2 hanger yoke is found sheared off. What is the main risk?
options: A cylinder of another gas could be attached, delivering the wrong gas
The yoke check valve can't seat, so O2 transfills
The first-stage regulator will pass full cylinder pressure
The O2 cylinder won't seat, so no backup O2 is available
questions.explanation: PISS depends on matching pins and holes to ensure the correct cylinder connection. With a pin missing, a wrong cylinder could fit, and the lecture lists incorrect gas administration, leaks, equipment damage, and patient injury as risks of improper attachment.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10)

questions.stem: The capnogram suddenly goes flat at zero. SpO2 is 99%, BP is unchanged, and PIP and exhaled tidal volume are unchanged. What is the most likely cause?
options: Cardiac arrest
Massive pulmonary embolism
Sampling line disconnection or kink
Esophageal migration of the tube
questions.explanation: Sudden waveform loss requires checking the airway, circuit, pulmonary blood flow, and sampling integrity. Stable BP rules against PE and arrest, and unchanged PIP and exhaled volume show the patient is still being ventilated through the tube. A sampling line problem is left.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 41, 50 (PDF p. 41, 51)

questions.stem: Right after a vaporizer is swapped on the manifold, the low-pressure leak check fails. The filler cap is confirmed closed. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The O2 fail-safe valve is leaking
The vaporizer's temperature compensation strip is stuck
The vaporizer isn't seated properly on the manifold
The pipeline inlet check valve is stuck open
questions.explanation: Slide 73 lists improper seating on the manifold, an incompatible vaporizer, and interlock failure as installation problems; the fix is ensuring correct installation before use. With the cap already checked, seating is left. The fail-safe and pipeline check valve are upstream of the low-pressure system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 69, 73 (PDF p. 35, 37)

questions.stem: A child is ventilated through an uncuffed tube that's too small, with a large audible leak. Which consequences follow? Select 2.
options: Inspired CO2 rises from rebreathing
Anesthetic gas spills into the OR
Delivered tidal volume increases
Compound A production increases
ETCO2 reads falsely low
Peak inspiratory pressure rises
questions.explanation: An uncuffed tube too small for the trachea lets anesthetic gas leak into the room (CO2 lecture, slide 14). ETT leaks also appear in Box 18.1 among equipment causes of decreased ETCO2. A leak lowers pressure and delivered volume, and it doesn't cause rebreathing.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 7); CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7); Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 43 (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Each agent is run at 1 MAC with the same fresh gas flow for one hour. Which uses the most liquid agent?
options: Desflurane
Sevoflurane
Isoflurane
Halothane
questions.explanation: Liquid used (mL/hr) = vol% x FGF x 3, so it scales with the dialed percent. MAC at age 40: des 6.6%, sevo 1.8%, iso 1.17%, halothane 0.76%. Des needs the highest vol%, so it uses the most liquid.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 52 (PDF p. 25, 26)

questions.stem: The patient must be briefly disconnected from the circuit to reposition the tube. Which step does the lecture recommend FIRST to limit room contamination?
options: Turn off only the vaporizer and leave N2O running
Turn off fresh gas flow or use the pause fresh gas function
Close the APL valve to hold gas in the circuit
Increase fresh gas flow to dilute the agent
questions.explanation: When the circuit is disconnected, the lecture says to turn off fresh gas flows or use the 'pause fresh gas flow' function; otherwise anesthetic-laden gas flows into the room. Closing the APL doesn't stop gas pouring out the open Y-piece, and N2O left running still contaminates.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which events would be detected primarily through agent analysis on the gas monitor? Select 2.
options: Vaporizer malfunction or contamination
Anesthesia breathing circuit leak
Vaporizer overdose
Malignant hyperthermia crisis
Venous air embolism
Hypoxic gas in the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: From the lecture's analyzer table: vaporizer malfunction or contamination and vaporizer overdose show up on agent analysis. Circuit leaks show N2 and CO2, air embolism CO2 and N2, MH CO2, and circuit hypoxia O2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 42 (PDF p. 42)

questions.stem: After failed intubation and failed supraglottic airway rescue, the patient can't be oxygenated and SpO2 is falling rapidly. What is the next step?
options: Continued two-person mask ventilation with an OPA
Another direct laryngoscopy attempt with a Miller blade
Fiberoptic intubation through the failed SGA
Cricothyrotomy through the cricothyroid membrane
questions.explanation: Cricothyrotomy is a lifesaving emergency procedure and the final option for 'cannot intubate, cannot ventilate' in every airway algorithm. Once oxygenation has failed by all routes, further attempts at the same techniques delay oxygenation. Approaches: needle, percutaneous, or surgical.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 15 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: What do the wicks and baffles in a variable bypass vaporizer accomplish?
options: They trap liquid droplets to prevent the pumping effect
They slow chamber flow so less agent is picked up at high FGF
They cool the liquid to hold vapor pressure constant
They increase liquid surface area so chamber gas leaves fully saturated
questions.explanation: Baffles direct fresh gas toward wicks that draw liquid up from the reservoir and spread it over a larger surface area. That flow-over design ensures the chamber gas is saturated, which the dial's concentration calibration depends on.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 57 (PDF p. 29)

questions.stem: Why does N2O exist as a liquid in an E-cylinder at room temperature while O2 remains a gas?
options: N2O's critical temp (about 36 C) is above room temp; O2's (-118.6 C) is far below
N2O's boiling point is above room temperature, while O2's boiling point is below
O2's critical temp is above room temp, but it's filled below its liquefying pressure
N2O is filled to a much higher pressure than O2 is in an E-cylinder
questions.explanation: A gas can only be liquefied by pressure below its critical temperature. N2O's critical temperature (about 36 C) is above room temperature, so compressing it liquefies it. O2's is -118.6 C, the highest temperature at which O2 can exist as a liquid, so no pressure will liquefy it at room temperature. N2O's boiling point is -88 C, and its fill pressure (745 psig) is lower than O2's.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 11, 14 (PDF p. 6, 7)

questions.stem: When BP is estimated by palpation during cuff deflation, which value is obtained?
options: Mean pressure, at maximal pulse amplitude
Pulse pressure, from the change in pulse strength
Diastolic pressure, when the pulse becomes strongest
Systolic pressure, at the return of the pulse
questions.explanation: Palpation estimates systolic pressure from the return of the pulse as the cuff deflates; Korotkoff sounds estimate systolic and diastolic. Maximal oscillation amplitude corresponds to MAP in oscillometric devices.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 86 (PDF p. 87)

questions.stem: An open-reservoir scavenging interface is connected to a vacuum source with too little flow for the waste gas volume. What happens?
options: Waste gas spills into the OR through the open relief ports
The pop-off valve opens to protect the circuit
Positive pressure builds in the breathing circuit
Negative pressure pulls gas from the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: The open interface has ports open to atmosphere, so it can't build positive or negative pressure on the circuit. If disposal flow is inadequate, the system is overloaded and waste gas spills into the room through those ports. Pop-off valves belong to the closed interface.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 13, 20 (PDF p. 7, 10)

questions.stem: Shortly after the patient is turned prone, this pressure-volume loop appears. Which problem does it MOST likely represent?
options: Abnormally increased compliance, as in emphysema
Increased inspiratory resistance, as from a kinked or bitten ETT
Increased expiratory resistance, as in bronchospasm
A leak in the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: The loop is closed but widened, with the inspiratory limb bowed toward the pressure axis. That's the lecture's pattern for increased resistance on inspiration (kinked or bitten ETT). Bronchospasm bows the expiratory limb, a leak leaves the loop open, and emphysema makes it tall and steep.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 29 (PDF p. 29)

questions.stem: The O2 pipeline hose is disconnected and the O2 cylinder is opened. Why doesn't cylinder O2 escape out through the machine's pipeline inlet?
options: The fail-safe valve blocks backflow into the pipeline
The pipeline inlet check valve is pushed into its seated position
The yoke check valve seats against the pipeline side
The first-stage regulator closes the pipeline inlet
questions.explanation: The pipeline inlet check valve is open when pipeline pressure pushes it forward. With the pipeline disconnected and a cylinder open, gas pressure pushes it backward into the seated position, reducing loss from backflow. The yoke check valve does the same job between cylinders, not at the pipeline inlet.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 31 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: The arterial line suddenly reads 58/40 with a flattened waveform. The patient's color and ETCO2 are unchanged. What is the FIRST action?
options: Check the line (flush, kinks, stopcocks, level), then confirm with a cuff
Give a vasopressor bolus now, then check the arterial line
Re-zero the transducer after lowering it to floor level
Replace the arterial catheter at a new cannulation site
questions.explanation: Before treating an abrupt pressure change, the lecture says to verify leveling, tubing, catheter patency, and waveform fidelity. A flattened (dampened) trace with a stable ETCO2 suggests a line problem; confirm with an independent measurement. Lowering the transducer would falsely RAISE readings.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 66 (PDF p. 67)

questions.stem: Which combination is expected to produce the MOST carbon monoxide?
options: Isoflurane with desiccated soda lime at room temperature
Sevoflurane with desiccated barium hydroxide lime
Desflurane with desiccated barium hydroxide lime at high temperature
Desflurane with fully hydrated soda lime
questions.explanation: CO production rises with the agent (des > enflurane > iso), desiccation, higher temperature, higher agent concentration, and barium hydroxide lime (Baralyme) instead of soda lime. Sevo forms no CO, and hydrated absorbent limits CO production.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 6, 7 (PDF p. 3, 4)

questions.stem: During laser surgery of the airway, which factors determine whether an endotracheal tube ignites? Select 3.
options: Tube material
Tube length
Concentration of O2 or N2O
Cuff inflation pressure
Direct contact of the heat source
Tidal volume setting
questions.explanation: Ignition relates to the tube material (PVC is flammable), the concentration of O2 or nitrous oxide, and direct contact of the heat source. That's why laser-resistant tubes are used, oxidizer concentration is limited, and cuffs are filled with saline or water and dye.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: A ventilated COPD patient develops auto-PEEP from inadequate expiratory time. How is ETCO2 likely to change?
options: Increase, from trapped CO2-rich gas
No change, since auto-PEEP affects only oxygenation
Decrease, from reduced CO2 delivery to the lungs
Increase, from higher CO2 production
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists auto-PEEP under decreased CO2 delivery or production (with hypotension, hypovolemia, PE, and V/Q mismatch). Trapped gas raises intrathoracic pressure, which impairs venous return and pulmonary perfusion, so less CO2 reaches the alveoli to be exhaled.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 43 (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: During CPR, the intubated patient's capnogram changes as shown. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: Hyperventilation from overly rapid bagging
Return of spontaneous circulation
Esophageal migration of the tube
Sampling line disconnection
questions.explanation: Low, flat CO2 waves during CPR reflect low pulmonary blood flow. A sudden rise in ETCO2 is the lecture's sign of ROSC, as CO2-rich blood reaches the lungs again. Hyperventilation lowers ETCO2, and esophageal placement or a disconnection would make CO2 fade or vanish, not jump.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 46 (PDF p. 47)

questions.stem: Running on the backup O2 cylinder, the gauge falls from 2000 to 500 psig, yet flowmeter flow stays constant. Which component makes this possible?
options: First-stage pressure regulator
O2 flush valve
Second-stage O2 pressure regulator
Yoke check valve
questions.explanation: The first-stage regulator, just downstream of the yoke, turns high, variable cylinder pressure into a steady (about 45 psi) output, protecting components and keeping flow stable as the cylinder empties. The second-stage regulator works on pressure that the first stage has already reduced.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 24 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: A conscious patient receives light-to-moderate sedation for a brief procedure. What does the lecture say about continuous temperature monitoring?
options: It is often uninformative, since thermoregulation is intact
It is required for every sedation case
It is contraindicated in conscious patients
It is useful only with a skin temperature probe
questions.explanation: There are no absolute contraindications to temperature monitoring, but in conscious patients or those with light-to-moderate sedation and intact thermoregulation, continuous monitoring is often uninformative. The standard calls for monitoring when significant changes are intended, anticipated, or suspected.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 83 (PDF p. 84)

questions.stem: In this circle system, the arrows show flow direction. In which quadrant is the CO2 absorber almost always placed?
options: Quadrant A
Quadrant B
Quadrant C
Quadrant D
questions.explanation: The inspiratory limb is the one carrying gas toward the patient (top arrow), and quadrant A is its bag side. The absorber is almost always placed there, so assisted or controlled ventilation can overcome its resistance to inspiration. B is the inspiratory limb on the patient side; C and D are the expiratory limb.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Which adjunct monitors are paired with the correct use or timing? Select 3.
options: Cerebral oximetry: carotid surgery
Precordial stethoscope: pediatrics
BIS: start after induction to avoid artifact
Precordial stethoscope: replaces capnography in adults
BIS: start while awake for a baseline
Cerebral oximetry: routine peripheral surgery
questions.explanation: Slide 53 lists cerebral oximetry for carotid surgery, BIS (instructor: start while the patient is awake to get a baseline), and a precordial stethoscope for pediatrics. Nothing in the lecture replaces capnography.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 53 (PDF p. 54)

questions.stem: During ongoing blood loss, ETCO2 drifts from 38 to 28 mmHg over 20 minutes with a normal waveform. Ventilator settings haven't changed, and BP is steadily falling. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Hyperventilation from light anesthesia
Decreased perfusion reducing CO2 delivery to the lungs
A sampling line leak diluting the sample
Exhausted CO2 absorbent
questions.explanation: With ventilation fixed, falling ETCO2 alongside falling BP points to decreased CO2 delivery: hypotension, hypovolemia, low cardiac output (slide 46: decreased perfusion). Hyperventilation requires increased ventilation, and an exhausted absorbent RAISES the baseline and ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 43, 46 (PDF p. 43, 47)

questions.stem: Fresh gas flow is lowered from 4 L/min to 1 L/min for the rest of a long case. How does this affect the absorbent?
options: It will be exhausted sooner, because more exhaled gas is rebreathed through it
It will last longer, because less fresh gas passes through it
Its life won't change, because only minute ventilation matters
It will last longer, because lower flow reduces channeling
questions.explanation: At low FGF, more exhaled gas is recirculated through the absorber, so it removes more CO2 and exhausts sooner. The lecture tells providers to understand how the chosen FGF affects how long a charge of soda lime lasts, and notes the absorber is required for low-flow technique.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 4, 8 (PDF p. 2, 4)

questions.stem: A canister under intense OR lighting shows no color change despite hours of use, and inspired CO2 is rising. What explains the missing color change?
options: Channeling keeps all granules equally fresh
Ethyl violet can be bleached by intense light
Ethyl violet only changes color at high fresh gas flows
The dye changes color only when compound A forms
questions.explanation: Ethyl violet changes from white to purple as pH falls, but the lecture notes it can be bleached by intense light, so an exhausted canister may not look purple. Channeling does the opposite of keeping granules equally fresh: it exhausts one path while the rest look unused.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: A fast-flush test shows a slow return to baseline with no oscillations, and the waveform looks rounded. What should you expect, and what should you check?
options: Underdamping underestimating SBP; add extension tubing
Underdamping overestimating SBP; check for bubbles, clot, or kinks
Overdamping underestimating SBP; check for bubbles, clot, or kinks
Overdamping overestimating SBP; lower the transducer
questions.explanation: The fast-flush test gauges damping from the resonant waves after the flush. No oscillations and a slow return mean an overdamped system, which underestimates SBP. Air bubbles, clot, kinks, excess tubing, and stopcocks degrade fidelity; extension tubing makes it worse.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 65, 69 (PDF p. 66, 70)

questions.stem: O2 supply pressure drifts down to 27 psig during a case with N2O running. What is the fail-safe valve doing to N2O flow?
options: Leaving it unchanged until 20 psig
Stopping it completely
Proportionally reducing it
Increasing it to keep total flow constant
questions.explanation: As O2 supply pressure falls below about 25-30 psig, the fail-safe proportionally reduces other gas flows. It stops them completely only below about 20 psig. It never raises N2O flow.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 34 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: For a 3-hour case, which inhaled technique best follows the lecture's environmental recommendations?
options: Isoflurane with high fresh gas flow for faster titration
Sevoflurane with low fresh gas flow in air/O2
Desflurane with low fresh gas flow in air/O2
Sevoflurane with N2O as the carrier gas
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends avoiding N2O as a carrier, avoiding unnecessarily high FGF, reserving des and N2O for cases where they improve outcomes, and using the more soluble agents (iso, sevo). Des still persists about 14 years in the atmosphere even at low flow; sevo about 1.1 years.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 22, 23 (PDF p. 11, 12)

questions.stem: A vaporizer is moved from a cold storage room into a warm OR and the liquid agent warms. What does the bimetallic strip do to the splitting ratio?
options: Sends more fresh gas through the chamber and less through the bypass
Keeps the splitting ratio fixed, since the dial sets it
Closes the chamber completely until temperature falls
Sends less fresh gas through the chamber and more through the bypass
questions.explanation: Warmer liquid has a higher vapor pressure, so each mL of chamber gas carries more agent. The bimetallic strip adjusts the splitting ratio in the opposite direction from cooling, sending less gas through the chamber so output stays at the dialed concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 56 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: A pregnant CRNA asks what the 1974 reports found in women exposed to waste anesthetic gases. Which findings were reported? Select 3.
options: Hepatic disease without any change in cancer
Liver and kidney disease
Spontaneous abortion
Reduced fertility
Congenital abnormalities in their offspring
Hearing loss
questions.explanation: Exposed women showed more spontaneous abortion, liver and kidney disease, cancer, and congenital abnormalities in offspring. 'Hepatic disease without a change in cancer' describes the exposed MEN. Hearing loss and fertility weren't among the reported findings.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: You are watching ST trends for ischemia during vascular surgery. Based on Landesberg's data, which ECG change should you expect most ischemic events to show?
options: New T-wave inversion alone
New Q waves
ST elevation
ST depression
questions.explanation: 97% of ischemic events in that study were ST depression, not elevation. V3 was the most sensitive lead (86.8%), then V4 and V5. That's why ST monitoring and lead selection are part of ECG setup.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 58 (PDF p. 59)

questions.stem: Mid-case, the O2 pipeline hose is pulled from the wall and the O2 supply low-pressure alarm sounds. The backup O2 cylinder is closed. What is the FIRST action?
options: Open the backup O2 cylinder on the machine
Press the O2 flush to keep the bag full
Increase N2O flow to maintain total fresh gas flow
Switch the patient to the auxiliary O2 flowmeter
questions.explanation: The machine uses the cylinder (regulated to about 45 psi) whenever pipeline pressure is lower, but only if the cylinder is open. The flush and the auxiliary flowmeter draw from the same O2 supply that just failed, and the fail-safe will reduce and then stop N2O as O2 pressure falls.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 26, 33, 44 (PDF p. 13, 17, 22)

questions.stem: A patient with significant methemoglobinemia on room air has a true arterial saturation of 70%. What will a standard pulse oximeter most likely display?
options: About 99%, because MetHb reads as oxyhemoglobin
About 55%, underestimating the true saturation
About 85%, overestimating the true saturation
About 70%, accurately reflecting saturation
questions.explanation: MetHb absorbs red and infrared light about equally (a 1:1 ratio), which the oximeter reads as about 85%. Below that true saturation, SpO2 overestimates; above it, SpO2 underestimates. Co-oximetry measures MetHb directly.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 75 (PDF p. 76)
questions.disc: Slide 75 places the over/underestimation crossover at 70%. Standard references (e.g., OpenAnesthesia) use 85%, matching the slide's own 1:1 = about 85% point. This question uses 85%.

questions.stem: Which leaks would a low-pressure system leak check be able to detect? Select 2.
options: A cracked flowmeter tube
A defective N2O pipeline quick connect
A loose vaporizer filler cap
A leaking N2O cylinder valve
A worn O2 cylinder yoke washer
A leak at the first-stage regulator
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system runs from the flow control valves to the common gas outlet: flowmeters, vaporizers, check valves, and the outlet. A filler cap and a cracked flowmeter tube sit inside it. Yoke washers, cylinder valves, quick connects, and the first-stage regulator are in the high or intermediate systems.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 39, 48, 69 (PDF p. 20, 24, 35)

questions.stem: In a bulk liquid O2 supply system, what converts the stored liquid to gas before it reaches the pipeline regulator?
options: A vaporizer and superheater downstream of the tank
The pipeline zone valve
The safety relief valve on the tank
The machine's first-stage regulator
questions.explanation: The lecture's bulk tank diagram shows liquid O2 at about -160 C in a vacuum-insulated tank; liquid passes through a control valve, vaporizer, and superheater, then a pressure regulator drops it to about 50 psig for the pipeline. The relief valve protects the tank from overpressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 32 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: A hypothermic, alkalotic patient has an SpO2 of 99%. What does the dissociation curve imply about tissue oxygenation?
options: The curve shifts left, so hemoglobin unloads O2 to tissues less readily
The curve shifts left, so SpO2 overestimates arterial PaO2 only
SpO2 of 99% guarantees adequate tissue oxygenation
The curve shifts right, so tissue O2 delivery is improved
questions.explanation: Right shifts (hypercapnia, acidosis, hyperthermia) lower Hb's O2 affinity and improve tissue delivery. Hypothermia and alkalosis do the opposite: a left shift, with Hb holding O2 tightly. Pulse oximetry also doesn't measure tissue O2 delivery or utilization.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 74, 76 (PDF p. 75, 77)

questions.stem: What handling advantage does a GE Aladin cassette have over a variable bypass vaporizer?
options: It keeps delivering agent if power fails
It works without a CPU to identify the agent
It doesn't need an agent-specific key to fill
It can be stored or handled in any position
questions.explanation: The Aladin cassette is removable and may be stored or handled in any position, so the tipping problem of variable bypass vaporizers doesn't apply. It still uses a key fill system, depends on the machine's CPU, and is identified by a magnetic code.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 66 (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: With ventilator settings unchanged, ETCO2 falls. Which conditions could explain it by reducing CO2 production or pulmonary CO2 delivery? Select 3.
options: Hypothermia
Pulmonary embolism
Hypotension
Hypoventilation
Sepsis
Malignant hyperthermia
questions.explanation: Decreased CO2 production or delivery: hypothermia, hypometabolism, pulmonary hypoperfusion, low cardiac output, PE, hemorrhage, hypotension, hypovolemia. MH and sepsis raise production, and hypoventilation raises ETCO2 by reducing elimination.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 43, 51 (PDF p. 43, 52)

questions.stem: Early in a case with fresh absorbent, the canister feels warm. What does this MOST likely reflect?
options: Normal heat from the neutralization reaction
Compound A breakdown releasing heat
Exhaustion of all hydroxides in the canister
Carbon monoxide formation from dry absorbent
questions.explanation: CO2 hydrates to carbonic acid, which reacts with metal hydroxides in a neutralization reaction producing water, carbonate, and HEAT. Warmth during active absorption is expected. An exhausted canister stops reacting, so it wouldn't be generating new heat.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 2 (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: During active rewarming after a long case, which temperature site is most likely to lag behind the true core temperature?
options: Pulmonary artery blood
Rectum
Nasopharynx
Distal esophagus
questions.explanation: Core temperature can be estimated at several sites, but during active cooling or rewarming, rectal temperature can lag behind faster-changing core sites. PA blood temperature is a strong core estimate, and the distal esophagus and nasopharynx track core closely.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 81 (PDF p. 82)

questions.stem: In a healthy supine patient under GA, an ABG shows PaCO2 42 mmHg with ETCO2 38 mmHg. How should this be interpreted?
options: Normal gradient; ETCO2 is tracking PaCO2 appropriately
Reversed gradient suggesting rebreathing
Widened gradient from increased alveolar dead space
Sampling error, since ETCO2 should equal PaCO2
questions.explanation: During routine GA in healthy supine patients, the PaCO2-ETCO2 gradient is typically about 5 mmHg (range 2-10). A 4 mmHg gap is normal. Widening beyond that suggests dead space or V/Q mismatch (PE, low cardiac output, OLV).
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 40 (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: Which flowmeter design features specifically reduce the risk of delivering a hypoxic mixture? Select 2.
options: Each tube calibrated for its specific gas
O2 flowmeter positioned last, closest to the outlet
Indicator read at its widest part
Counterclockwise rotation to increase flow
O2 knob larger and fluted so it can be identified by touch
Laminar flow at low flow rates
questions.explanation: O2 last means an upstream leak loses another gas instead of O2, and the larger fluted O2 knob is a tactile safety feature. Gas-specific calibration and reading the widest part are about accuracy; laminar flow and knob direction are normal operation.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 40, 41 (PDF p. 20, 21)

questions.stem: N2O is set at 3 L/min on a machine with a proportioning system that keeps FiO2 at least 25%. About what is the lowest O2 flow it will allow?
options: 0.5 L/min
0.75 L/min
1 L/min
1.5 L/min
questions.explanation: For O2 to be 25% of the total, O2 / (O2 + 3) = 0.25, so O2 = 1 L/min (1 of 4 L total). At 0.75 L/min, O2 would be 0.75/3.75 = 20%.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 45 (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: Which factors contribute to alarm fatigue? Select 3.
options: Evaluating the cause of every alarm
High numbers of noncritical or false alarms
Alarm limits set to meet practice standards
Alarms that interfere with team communication
Variable-pitch pulse oximeter tones
Difficulty locating alarms in a noisy environment
questions.explanation: Contributing factors on slide 19: many noncritical or false alarms, difficulty localizing or distinguishing alarms in noisy settings, and alarms interfering with communication. Results include ignoring or disabling alarms and missed critical events. Variable-pitch tones and evaluating every alarm are the recommended countermeasures.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 19 (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: An OPA is inserted in a patient who is only lightly sedated, and inspiratory stridor develops. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: The OPA caused dental damage with bleeding
The OPA stimulated laryngeal reflexes
The OPA pushed the tongue into the hypopharynx
The OPA is too small to lift the tongue
questions.explanation: The lecture lists stimulation of oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes as an OPA complication; in a light patient that can produce laryngospasm and stridor. That's why awake or lightly sedated patients tolerate NPAs better.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 5 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: A spontaneously breathing patient under sedation has significant metabolic acidosis. How would you expect ETCO2 to change?
options: No change, since metabolic disorders don't affect ETCO2
Increase, from compensatory hypoventilation
Increase, from higher CO2 production
Decrease, from compensatory hyperventilation
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists metabolic acidosis (if spontaneously breathing) under hyperventilation, which lowers ETCO2. Metabolic alkalosis in a spontaneously breathing patient causes hypoventilation and raises ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 43 (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Pipeline O2 pressure fluctuates between 45 and 55 psig, yet the O2 flowmeter setting stays steady. Which component is responsible?
options: O2 fail-safe valve
First-stage (cylinder) pressure regulator
Second-stage O2 pressure regulator
Pipeline inlet check valve
questions.explanation: The second-stage regulator further reduces pipeline or cylinder pressure (about 14-16 psi for O2) and dampens fluctuations, so flowmeter settings stay steady. The first-stage regulator only handles cylinder gas, and check valves and the fail-safe don't smooth pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: Which OR air sampling results exceed the NIOSH recommended limits? Select 3.
options: N2O as the sole agent at 30 ppm TWA
Sevoflurane 3 ppm, no N2O in use
Desflurane 1.5 ppm, no N2O in use
N2O as the sole agent at 20 ppm TWA
Isoflurane 1 ppm during a combined isoflurane/N2O anesthetic
Sevoflurane 0.4 ppm during a combined sevoflurane/N2O anesthetic
questions.explanation: Halogenated agent used alone: no more than 2 ppm, so sevo 3 ppm exceeds it and des 1.5 ppm doesn't. N2O as the sole agent: no more than 25 ppm TWA, so 30 exceeds it and 20 doesn't. When a halogenated agent is combined with N2O, its limit drops to 0.5 ppm, so iso at 1 ppm exceeds it while sevo at 0.4 ppm doesn't.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)
questions.supp: The combined-use limit (0.5 ppm halogenated with N2O at 25 ppm; halogenated limit is a ceiling over a sampling period up to 1 hour) comes from NIOSH's 1977 recommendation. Slide 10 lists only the 2 ppm and 25 ppm values.

questions.stem: A premature infant has a suspected patent ductus arteriosus. Where should the NIBP cuff go to best reflect cerebral perfusion?
options: Left arm
Right leg
Left leg
Right arm
questions.explanation: When ductal shunting is a concern in premature infants, right-arm (preductal) pressure best approximates cerebral perfusion. The left arm may be partly postductal, and the legs are postductal. Instructor note: premature infant, put BP cuff on R arm.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 90 (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: You smell volatile agent near the machine and the bag is slow to refill. The vaporizer was just filled. What is the FIRST thing to check?
options: That the O2 cylinder yoke washer is present
That the scavenger interface is connected
That the vaporizer filler cap is replaced and tight
That the vaporizer dial isn't set above 5%
questions.explanation: Slide 69: a loose or missing filler cap causes a vaporizer leak that a low-pressure check may detect. The intervention is always checking that the cap is replaced and closed tightly. Scavenger problems don't cause a low-pressure leak, and the yoke washer is in the high-pressure system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 69 (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Gas flows preferentially along the smooth wall of a CO2 absorber canister. What is the MOST likely consequence?
options: The indicator changes color evenly throughout the canister
Absorbent along the flow path exhausts early while color elsewhere looks fresh
CO2 absorption improves because wall contact increases surface area
Resistance to gas flow rises across the whole canister
questions.explanation: Channeling is flow moving preferentially along the canister sides (between the smooth wall and irregular granules) and within the absorbent. Gas bypasses much of the absorbent, so the used path exhausts while the rest can look fresh. That's one reason color change isn't reliable. Channeling follows the path of LEAST resistance, so it doesn't raise resistance.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 4, 5 (PDF p. 2, 3)

questions.stem: At 20 C and 1 atm, what concentration of isoflurane leaves the vaporizing chamber of a variable bypass vaporizer before it mixes with bypass gas?
options: About 21%
About 32%
About 48%
About 88%
questions.explanation: Chamber gas is fully saturated, so its concentration equals vapor pressure divided by atmospheric pressure: 240/760 is about 32% for iso. Sevo is 160/760, about 21% (the lecture's example); des would be 669/760, about 88%. The dial sets how much bypass gas dilutes this.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 53 (PDF p. 25, 27)

questions.stem: A patient in cardiac arrest is intubated. Breath sounds are bilateral and the chest rises, but ETCO2 is very low with small waveforms. What is the best interpretation?
options: Hyperventilation is lowering ETCO2; reduce the rate
Low ETCO2 proves esophageal placement; reintubate immediately
The tube is likely tracheal; low ETCO2 reflects low pulmonary blood flow
The sampling line is kinked; replace it before continuing
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists low cardiac output or arrest under decreased CO2 delivery. With bilateral breath sounds, chest rise, and persistent (if small) waveforms, placement is supported; the low value reflects limited pulmonary flow. That's why compression quality is judged by trying to keep ETCO2 at least 10 mmHg.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 43, 93 (PDF p. 43, 94)

questions.stem: After CO2 insufflation for laparoscopy, the flow-volume loop keeps its normal shape but covers a smaller volume. What is the best interpretation?
options: A leak around the endotracheal tube cuff
Bronchospasm producing an obstructive pattern
Insufflation producing a restrictive pattern
New onset of pulmonary fibrosis
questions.explanation: Instructor note on slide 46: insufflating the abdomen mimics a restrictive pattern. Restrictive loops keep their shape at smaller volumes; obstructive loops show reduced expiratory flow at larger volumes. The timing points to insufflation, not new lung disease.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 30, 46 (PDF p. 30, 47)

questions.stem: A large leak exists at a vaporizer mount, and the bag won't fill with 3 L/min from the flowmeters. Why does pressing the O2 flush still fill the bag quickly?
options: The flush reroutes gas through the auxiliary flowmeter
The flush closes the outlet check valve behind the leak
The flush bypasses the flowmeters and vaporizers
The flush raises flowmeter pressure enough to seal the leak
questions.explanation: The flush sits at the end of the intermediate system and sends O2 directly to the common gas outlet, bypassing the low-pressure system (flowmeters and vaporizers). A low-pressure leak therefore doesn't affect it. Keep in mind the flush delivers O2 without agent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 36, 39 (PDF p. 18, 20)

questions.stem: Which airway items are part of the lecture's MS MAID room setup? Select 3.
options: An LMA
A fiberoptic tower
An additional blade and handle
A jet ventilation setup
A double-lumen tube
OPA and NPA
questions.explanation: Airway in MS MAID: primary opened and ready, backup packaged but within reach: LMA, additional blade and handle, ETT sizes plus or minus, flexible stylet, lubrication, 10 mL syringe, OPA, and NPA. Instructor notes: GETA, backup to everything; always have an LMA around.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: During a period of rapidly changing hemodynamics, why may NIBP cycling every 5 minutes fall short?
options: Cuffs cycled every 5 minutes cause falsely low readings
The ASA standard requires continuous BP during all changes
Oscillometric devices lose accuracy at any interval over 1 minute
Evidence suggests NIBP's predictive usefulness declines when intervals exceed about 3 minutes
questions.explanation: Slide 91 notes evidence that NIBP's predictive usefulness may begin to decline when measurement intervals exceed about 3 minutes during changing hemodynamics. The ASA minimum is at least every 5 minutes, which is a floor, not a guarantee for unstable patients.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 90 (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: In a well-preoxygenated patient during apnea, SpO2 falls from 100% to 97%. What does this suggest about PaO2?
options: PaO2 is now near 60 mmHg, at the steep part of the curve
PaO2 may already have fallen a lot, since the upper curve is flat
PaO2 can't change while SpO2 stays above 95%
PaO2 has fallen only slightly, since SpO2 changed only 3%
questions.explanation: The upper oxyhemoglobin curve is flat, so large drops in PaO2 produce only small changes in SpO2. Once PaO2 reaches the steep portion (around 60 mmHg = about 90%), desaturation accelerates. A small SpO2 dip from 100% can hide a big PaO2 fall.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 76 (PDF p. 77)

questions.stem: Condensation collects inside the absorber canister during a long low-flow case. Where does this water come from?
options: Water condensing from dry medical-grade O2
Water released from calcium carbonate as it forms
Water produced by the neutralization reactions, plus exhaled humidity
Water leaking from the scavenging interface
questions.explanation: Carbonic acid reacting with the hydroxides forms water, carbonate, and heat, and the absorbent also conserves exhaled humidity, more so at low flows. Medical gases are dry, so they aren't the source.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 2, 3 (PDF p. 1, 2)

questions.stem: A delayed transport runs on a full O2 E-cylinder, and the patient needs a non-rebreather at 15 L/min. Roughly how many minutes of O2 are available?
options: About 22 minutes
About 44 minutes
About 66 minutes
About 127 minutes
questions.explanation: A full O2 E-cylinder holds about 660 L. 660 L divided by 15 L/min is about 44 minutes. 127 minutes would come from mistakenly using gauge psig divided by 15.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 12, 13 (PDF p. 6, 7)

questions.stem: A leak in the ventilator's bellows reduces the tidal volume actually delivered. How is ETCO2 likely to change?
options: Increase, from hypoventilation
Decrease, from increased dead space
Decrease, from dilution with room air
No change, since the circuit is still sealed
questions.explanation: Box 18.1 lists ventilator leak among equipment causes of INCREASED ETCO2: less delivered volume means less CO2 eliminated. Circuit or ETT leaks that entrain room air around the sample are the ones listed under decreased ETCO2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 43 (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Which breathing circuit component does the lecture flag as especially prone to leaks from manufacturing imperfections?
options: Disposable circuits, especially the swivel type
Reusable rubber reservoir bags
The Y-piece of a reusable circuit
Unidirectional valve discs
questions.explanation: Low-pressure leaks can come from breaks in rubber and plastic components, loose unidirectional valve domes, or disposable circuits. The lecture singles out swivel-type disposable circuits as particularly prone to leaks from manufacturing imperfections.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which are the more common arterial monitoring sites in pediatric and neonatal anesthesia? Select 3.
options: Axillary artery
Brachial artery
Dorsalis pedis artery
Radial artery
Umbilical artery
Femoral artery
questions.explanation: The lecture lists the umbilical, radial, and femoral arteries as three of the more common pediatric and neonatal sites. In critically ill newborns, the umbilical artery is convenient for pressure monitoring and blood sampling.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 71 (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: O2 supply pressure starts to fall during a case. What tells the provider, and what acts on the gas mixture?
options: The fail-safe alarms; the proportioning system reduces N2O flow
The O2 analyzer alarms; the second-stage regulator stops N2O
The O2 supply low-pressure alarm alerts; the fail-safe reduces N2O flow
The proportioning system alarms; the fail-safe raises O2 flow
questions.explanation: The machine roadmap shows a dedicated O2 supply low-pressure alarm in the intermediate system to alert the provider. The fail-safe, in the N2O line, silently proportions and then stops N2O as O2 pressure falls. The proportioning system responds to flow settings, not supply pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 34 (PDF p. 3, 17)

questions.stem: Which indexing system pairings are correct? Select 2.
options: Quick connect: nationally standardized cylinder fitting
DISS: E-cylinder valve to hanger yoke
PISS: pipeline hose connection to the machine
PISS: vaporizer to manifold
PISS: E-cylinder valve to hanger yoke
DISS: pipeline hose connection to the machine
questions.explanation: PISS matches pin holes on the cylinder valve to pins on the yoke. DISS gives gas-specific diameters on a nationally standardized thread for pipeline connections. Quick connectors are wall fittings that are NOT standardized between manufacturers. Vaporizers use their own manifold and interlock systems.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 29, 30 (PDF p. 9, 15)

questions.stem: A patient with severe peripheral vascular disease has NIBP readings of 158/82 in the right arm and 126/70 in the left. Which value should guide management?
options: The average of both arms
The lower reading, 126/70
Whichever arm is on the surgical side
The higher reading, 158/82
questions.explanation: In patients with severe peripheral vascular disease, there can be significant pressure differences between extremities, and the lecture says the greater value should be used.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 70 (PDF p. 71)

questions.stem: A PACU transport requires a non-rebreather at 15 L/min. Why isn't the machine's auxiliary O2 flowmeter the right source?
options: It delivers only through the breathing circuit
It is supplied only by the backup cylinder
It delivers only up to about 10 L/min
It is limited to 2 L/min by the proportioning system
questions.explanation: The auxiliary O2 flowmeter provides supplemental O2 (cannula, mask, Ambu bag) with the circuit left intact, at flows up to about 10 L/min, from the same pipeline source. A 15 L/min non-rebreather exceeds that.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 44 (PDF p. 22)

questions.stem: During bag-mask ventilation, peak airway pressure is high while exhaled tidal volume is minimal. What does this combination indicate?
options: A large leak around the mask
Adequate ventilation with a good seal
Obstruction limiting gas movement
Hyperventilation from excess bag pressure
questions.explanation: Peak airway pressure and exhaled tidal volume are among the lecture's objective measures of BVM adequacy. High pressure with little volume returned means gas isn't moving, which points to obstruction. A large mask leak gives LOW pressure along with low volume.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: On a hot day, the OR temperature reaches 24 C. Which agent could boil at that room temperature at 1 atm?
options: Sevoflurane
Isoflurane
Halothane
Desflurane
questions.explanation: Boiling points at 1 atm: des 22.8 C, iso 48.5 C, halothane 50.2 C, sevo 58.6 C. Only des boils below 24 C, which is why its vaporizer heats and pressurizes the agent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 60 (PDF p. 25, 30)

questions.stem: For short cases, what does the lecture recommend to reduce environmental impact without slowing emergence?
options: Raise fresh gas flow at the end of the case to speed washout
Get practiced with iso and sevo to match the emergence of less soluble agents
Add N2O as the carrier gas to speed induction and emergence
Use desflurane at high flow so emergence and turnover are faster
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends becoming practiced with the more soluble agents (iso, sevo), even for shorter cases, to get emergence timing similar to the less soluble agents, while avoiding high FGF, N2O as a carrier, and routine desflurane.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: A procedure includes planned therapeutic cooling of the patient. How does the ASA temperature standard apply?
options: Only skin temperature is needed during planned cooling
Monitoring starts only if the patient shivers
Monitoring is optional, since cooling is deliberate
Temperature must be monitored because the change is intended
questions.explanation: ASA 2.4: every patient shall have temperature monitored when clinically significant changes are intended, anticipated, or suspected. Planned cooling is an intended change. Core sites are preferred; skin temperature doesn't represent mean body temperature.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 14, 83 (PDF p. 14, 84)

questions.stem: Which OR air sampling results exceed the NIOSH recommended limits? Select 3.
options: N2O as the sole agent at 20 ppm TWA
Isoflurane 1 ppm during a combined isoflurane/N2O anesthetic
N2O as the sole agent at 30 ppm TWA
Sevoflurane 3 ppm, no N2O in use
Sevoflurane 0.4 ppm during a combined sevoflurane/N2O anesthetic
Desflurane 1.5 ppm, no N2O in use
questions.explanation: Halogenated agent used alone: no more than 2 ppm, so sevo 3 ppm exceeds it and des 1.5 ppm doesn't. N2O as the sole agent: no more than 25 ppm TWA, so 30 exceeds it and 20 doesn't. When a halogenated agent is combined with N2O, its limit drops to 0.5 ppm, so iso at 1 ppm exceeds it while sevo at 0.4 ppm doesn't.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)
questions.supp: The combined-use limit (0.5 ppm halogenated with N2O at 25 ppm; halogenated limit is a ceiling over a sampling period up to 1 hour) comes from NIOSH's 1977 recommendation. Slide 10 lists only the 2 ppm and 25 ppm values.

questions.stem: Which numbered component reduces O2 pressure to about 14-16 psi before it reaches the O2 flow control valve?
options: Component 1
Component 2
Component 3
Component 5
questions.explanation: Component 2 is the second-stage O2 pressure regulator, which lowers pipeline or cylinder pressure to about 14-16 psi and dampens fluctuations. Component 3 is the N2O second-stage regulator (about 26-38 psi), 1 is the fail-safe, and 5 is the outlet check valve.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 33 (PDF p. 3, 17)

questions.stem: At the end of a volatile anesthetic, the patient is still deep. Which approach best limits waste gas exposure before extubation?
options: Disconnect and let the patient exhale into room ventilation
Squeeze the reservoir bag to empty the circuit, then extubate
Keep the patient connected to the scavenged circuit while agent washes out
Turn off FGF and remove the mask to let the patient breathe room air
questions.explanation: If a deeply anesthetized patient is disconnected, relatively high concentrations of agent are exhaled into the room (instructor: even a deep extubated patient is still breathing out gas). Emptying the circuit while disconnected also spills gas. Keeping the patient on the scavenged circuit sends exhaled agent to disposal.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: During ventilation of a patient with long-standing lung disease, this pressure-volume loop appears. What does it MOST likely show?
options: Abnormally increased compliance, as in emphysema
Increased inspiratory resistance from a kinked ETT
Decreased compliance from pneumothorax
A leak in the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: The loop is tall and steep, hugging the volume axis: large volume for little pressure, the lecture's pattern for abnormally increased compliance (emphysema). Decreased compliance shifts toward the pressure axis, a leak leaves the loop open, and a kink bows the inspiratory limb.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 28, 29 (PDF p. 28, 29)

questions.stem: Which statements about the reported clinical accuracy of pulse oximetry are correct? Select 2.
options: Unaffected by perfusion or temperature
No meaningful accuracy below 90% saturation
About plus or minus 1% across all saturations
About plus or minus 3% from 50-70% saturation
More accurate than laboratory co-oximetry
About plus or minus 2-3% from 70-100% saturation
questions.explanation: Reported accuracy is typically plus or minus 2-3% from 70-100% saturation and about plus or minus 3% from 50-70%. Readings below 90% are still usable. Co-oximetry is the reference standard, and perfusion and temperature both affect oximetry.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 76 (PDF p. 77)

questions.stem: What does the lecture recommend about nitrous oxide for labor analgesia?
options: Prefer it because its atmospheric life is short
Use it only with high fresh gas flow
Use it routinely, since exposure limits don't apply in labor
Reconsider routine use when alternatives exist
questions.explanation: N2O can persist up to 114 years in the atmosphere. The lecture recommends avoiding N2O as a carrier gas, reserving it for cases where it reduces morbidity or mortality, and reconsidering routine N2O for labor analgesia when alternatives exist.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Which features characterize an obstructive pattern on the flow-volume loop? Select 2.
options: Smaller volumes with a preserved shape
Reduced expiratory flow
Increased expiratory flow
Larger lung volumes
A tall, steep pressure-volume shape
A loop that doesn't close
questions.explanation: Obstructive disease (COPD, asthma) is trouble getting air out: expiratory flow falls (a scooped, steeper loop) at larger lung volumes. Smaller volumes with preserved shape is restrictive, an open loop is a leak, and a tall steep P-V loop is increased compliance.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 30 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: Which are among the nine components of an OR ventilation system? Select 3.
options: An exhaust port to the outside
The scavenging interface
Fresh air intake from outside
The CO2 absorber
The APL valve
A series of filters
questions.explanation: The nine: fresh air intake, central pump, filters, air conditioning units, a manifold distributing fresh air, a manifold collecting air, a fresh air inflow port in each OR, an exhaust port to the hospital air conditioning system, and an exhaust port to the outside. The interface, APL, and absorber belong to the anesthesia machine and scavenging system.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 15 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: A sevoflurane vaporizer is mistakenly filled with isoflurane and dialed to 2%. How will output compare with the dial?
options: Equal to the dial, because the splitting ratio is fixed
Equal to the dial, because temperature compensation corrects it
Higher than dialed, because iso's vapor pressure (240) exceeds sevo's (160)
Lower than dialed, because iso's vapor pressure is lower than sevo's
questions.explanation: The splitting ratio is calibrated to sevo's vapor pressure (160 mmHg), and ratios differ among agents based on vapor pressure. Iso's higher vapor pressure (240 mmHg) saturates chamber gas at a higher concentration, so output exceeds the dial. The lecture's intervention: always double-check bottle, key, and vaporizer.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 54 (PDF p. 25, 27)

questions.stem: During the morning check, the O2 cylinder is found open and pipeline pressure reads 42 psig. Over the first case, the cylinder gauge steadily falls. What is the best action?
options: Switch to the auxiliary O2 flowmeter to spare the cylinder
Close the cylinder to keep it as backup and report the low pipeline pressure
Increase O2 flowmeter settings to draw more from the pipeline
Leave the cylinder open, since it is supplementing a weak pipeline
questions.explanation: The machine draws from whichever source is at higher pressure. Pipeline normally runs 50-55 psi, above the cylinder's regulated ~45 psi. At 42 psig the open cylinder takes over and silently empties, leaving no backup. The auxiliary flowmeter draws from the same O2 supply.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: Per AANA Standard 5, when must anesthesia equipment function be verified?
options: Weekly by biomedical engineering
Once daily at the start of the first case
Only after the machine has been moved
Before each anesthetic
questions.explanation: AANA Standard 5: follow manufacturer instructions, institutional policy, and safety precautions for daily checks, and verify the function of anesthesia equipment prior to each anesthetic. Operate equipment to minimize fire, explosion, shock, and malfunction risk.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 16 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: Laryngoscopy gives a poor view. The head is extended, but the occiput is flat on the bed. Which correction matches the lecture's sniffing position?
options: Add a shoulder roll to increase extension of the cervical spine
Lower the head of the bed so the patient lies completely flat
Elevate the occiput and keep extension at the atlanto-occipital joint
Remove the head extension and flex the neck forward instead
questions.explanation: Sniffing position = elevating the occiput plus extending the head at the atlanto-occipital joint. With the occiput flat, the elevation piece is missing. A shoulder roll increases extension without the occiput elevation.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 3 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: ETCO2 keeps rising despite doubling minute ventilation. The absorbent is fresh, inspired CO2 is zero, and the patient is tachycardic. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Hypoventilation from a ventilator leak
Increased CO2 production, as in malignant hyperthermia
Absorption of insufflated CO2 during laparoscopy
Rebreathing from an incompetent expiratory valve
questions.explanation: Zero inspired CO2 rules out rebreathing, and doubled ventilation rules out simple hypoventilation. CO2 rising faster than you can blow it off points to increased production, and MH leads Box 18.1's list. With no insufflation described, laparoscopy doesn't fit.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slides 42, 43 (PDF p. 42, 43)

questions.stem: How does the gas analyzer measure N2O and volatile agents alongside CO2?
options: Paramagnetic analysis of each gas
Galvanic fuel cells specific to each agent
Mass calculation from inspired and expired O2
Infrared analysis at multiple wavelengths
questions.explanation: CO2 strongly absorbs infrared near 4.3 microns, and multiple wavelengths permit analysis of CO2, N2O, and potent volatile agents. IR analyzers use an infrared source, gas sampler, optical path, detector, and signal processor. Paramagnetic and galvanic methods measure O2.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 40 (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: During mask ventilation after induction, a chin lift, head extension, and jaw thrust are applied, but obstruction from the tongue persists. What is the next step from the lecture's airway tools?
options: Insert an oropharyngeal airway
Increase the O2 flush to overcome the obstruction
Flex the neck to open the posterior pharynx
Switch to cricoid pressure
questions.explanation: The tongue and soft palate are the main sources of obstruction. After the triple maneuver, an OPA follows the oropharyngeal curve and lifts the tongue, and it also helps the mask seal. Neck flexion worsens obstruction, and flushing only raises pressure.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 3, 5 (PDF p. 3, 5)

questions.stem: How does the GE Aladin system know which agent is in the cassette that has been inserted?
options: The gas analyzer identifies the agent after delivery starts
The key fill adapter signals the agent to the machine
The provider selects the agent on the vaporizer dial
The CPU reads a magnetic code on the cassette
questions.explanation: The Aladin's central processing unit identifies each cassette by its magnetic code, then electronically controls flow rates, bypass percentages, and temperature. The key fill system prevents misfilling the cassette itself.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 66 (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: During spontaneous ventilation, the conducting tubing between the APL valve and the scavenging interface comes apart. What happens?
options: The interface pop-in valve pulls room air into the circuit
Waste gas leaving the APL vents directly into the room
The breathing circuit loses pressure and the bag collapses
The ventilator relief valve takes over waste gas removal
questions.explanation: The conducting tubing carries waste gas from the APL (or ventilator relief valve) to the interface. If it's disconnected, gas exiting the APL has nowhere to go but the room. The circuit itself stays intact, and the ventilator relief valve only applies during mechanical ventilation.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10)

questions.stem: Which pairings correctly match each safety device to the change it responds to? Select 2.
options: Fail-safe valve: falling O2 supply pressure
Fail-safe valve: O2-to-N2O flow ratio at the flow control valves
Fail-safe valve: inspired O2 concentration
Proportioning system: inspired O2 concentration
Proportioning system: falling O2 supply pressure
Proportioning system: O2-to-N2O flow ratio at the flow control valves
questions.explanation: The fail-safe, in the N2O line, responds to falling O2 supply PRESSURE. The proportioning system links O2 and N2O at the flow control valves to keep FiO2 above about 25%. Neither measures O2 concentration, which is why crossed pipelines slip past both.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 34, 45 (PDF p. 17, 23)

questions.stem: A morbidly obese patient's flow-volume loop keeps a normal shape but covers a smaller volume. Which pattern is this?
options: Fixed upper airway obstruction
Obstructive, from trouble getting air out
Restrictive, from trouble expanding the lungs
Normal, since the shape is preserved
questions.explanation: Restrictive disease means trouble getting air in or expanding, giving smaller volumes; the lecture's examples are fibrosis and obesity. Obstructive disease shows reduced expiratory flow at larger volumes.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation (Stone): slide 30 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: For laser microlaryngoscopy with a laser-resistant tube, which gas choice best reduces ignition risk?
options: 100% O2 to maximize safety margin
Air/O2 at the lowest acceptable FiO2
O2/N2O to lower the O2 fraction
N2O with a small O2 fraction
questions.explanation: Ignition depends on tube material, the concentration of O2 or N2O, and direct heat contact. N2O supports combustion like O2, so swapping O2 for N2O doesn't lower risk. Air with the lowest acceptable FiO2 reduces the oxidizer concentration.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: Which vaporizer problems can leak anesthetic into the OR? Select 3.
options: Loose mounts
The interface pop-in valve opening
Exhausted CO2 absorbent
An open APL valve during spontaneous ventilation
Incompletely closed fill ports
Defective seals and gaskets
questions.explanation: Vaporizers are usually gas tight but occasionally leak through loose mounts, defective seals and gaskets, or incompletely closed fill ports. The APL is the normal exit for waste gas to the scavenger, and the pop-in valve draws room air INTO the scavenger.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Per the ASA circulation standard, how long must the ECG be continuously displayed?
options: From the start of anesthesia until preparing to leave the room
Only during periods of hemodynamic instability
From intubation until extubation is completed
From induction until the incision is closed
